 62class FFmpegNormalize:
 63    """
 64    ffmpeg-normalize class.
 65
 66    Args:
 67        normalization_type (str, optional): Normalization type. Defaults to "ebu".
 68        target_level (float, optional): Target level. Defaults to -23.0.
 69        print_stats (bool, optional): Print loudnorm stats. Defaults to False.
 70        print_summary (bool, optional): Print a before/after summary table to stderr after processing. Defaults to False.
 71        threshold (float, optional): When set to a positive value, skip normalization when the input is already within this many dB/LU of the target level, copying it through unchanged. Defaults to 0 (disabled, always normalize).
 72        loudness_range_target (float, optional): Loudness range target. Defaults to 7.0.
 73        keep_loudness_range_target (bool, optional): Keep loudness range target. Defaults to False.
 74        keep_lra_above_loudness_range_target (bool, optional): Keep input loudness range above loudness range target. Defaults to False.
 75        true_peak (float, optional): True peak. Defaults to -2.0.
 76        offset (float, optional): Offset. Defaults to 0.0.
 77        lower_only (bool, optional): Whether the audio should not increase in loudness. Defaults to False.
 78        auto_lower_loudness_target (bool, optional): Automatically lower EBU Integrated Loudness Target.
 79        dual_mono (bool, optional): Dual mono. Defaults to False.
 80        dynamic (bool, optional): Use dynamic EBU R128 normalization. This is a one-pass algorithm and skips the initial media scan. Defaults to False.
 81        audio_codec (str, optional): Audio codec. Defaults to "pcm_s16le".
 82        audio_bitrate (float, optional): Audio bitrate. Defaults to None.
 83        sample_rate (int, optional): Sample rate. Defaults to None.
 84        audio_channels (int | None, optional): Audio channels. Defaults to None.
 85        keep_original_audio (bool, optional): Keep original audio. Defaults to False.
 86        pre_filter (str, optional): Pre filter. Defaults to None.
 87        post_filter (str, optional): Post filter. Defaults to None.
 88        video_codec (str, optional): Video codec. Defaults to "copy".
 89        video_disable (bool, optional): Disable video. Defaults to False.
 90        subtitle_disable (bool, optional): Disable subtitles. Defaults to False.
 91        metadata_disable (bool, optional): Disable metadata. Defaults to False.
 92        chapters_disable (bool, optional): Disable chapters. Defaults to False.
 93        write_encoder_settings (bool, optional): Write the effective encoder settings (codec, bitrate, sample rate, channels and the normalization filter including the measured loudnorm values) as an ENCODER_SETTINGS tag on each normalized audio stream. Defaults to False.
 94        extra_input_options (list, optional): Extra input options. Defaults to None.
 95        extra_output_options (list, optional): Extra output options. Defaults to None.
 96        output_format (str, optional): Output format. Defaults to None.
 97        extension (str, optional): Output file extension to use for output files that were not explicitly specified. Defaults to "mkv".
 98        dry_run (bool, optional): Dry run. Defaults to False.
 99        debug (bool, optional): Debug. Defaults to False.
100        progress (bool, optional): Progress. Defaults to False.
101        replaygain (bool, optional): Write ReplayGain tags without normalizing. Defaults to False.
102        batch (bool, optional): Preserve relative loudness between files (album mode). Defaults to False.
103        audio_streams (list[int] | None, optional): List of audio stream indices to normalize. Defaults to None (all streams).
104        audio_default_only (bool, optional): Only normalize audio streams with default disposition. Defaults to False.
105        keep_other_audio (bool, optional): Keep non-selected audio streams in output (copy without normalization). Defaults to False.
106        keep_mtime (bool, optional): Copy the input file's modification time to the output file. Defaults to False.
107        keep_bit_depth (bool, optional): Carry the detected input bit depth through to the output encoder. Defaults to True.
108        verify (bool, optional): Measure the encoded output and check its effective target and peak ceiling. Defaults to False. Not available with ReplayGain; skipped during dry runs.
109        verify_loudness_tolerance (float, optional): Allowed level deviation in dB/LU. Defaults to 0.5.
110        verify_peak_tolerance (float, optional): Allowed peak overshoot in dB. Defaults to 0.1.
111
112    Raises:
113        FFmpegNormalizeError: If the ffmpeg executable is not found or does not support the loudnorm filter.
114    """

366    def add_media_file(self, input_file: str, output_file: str) -> None:
367        """
368        Add a media file to normalize
369
370        Args:
371            input_file (str): Path to input file
372            output_file (str): Path to output file
373        """
374        if not os.path.exists(input_file):
375            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(f"file {input_file} does not exist")
376
377        ext = os.path.splitext(output_file)[1][1:].lower()
378        if ext in PCM_INCOMPATIBLE_EXTS:
379            if self.audio_codec is not None and "pcm" in self.audio_codec:
380                raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
381                    f"Output extension {ext} does not support PCM audio. "
382                    "Please choose a suitable audio codec with the -c:a option."
383                )
384            if (
385                self.audio_codec is None
386                and get_muxer_default_audio_encoder(ext) is None
387            ):
388                raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
389                    f"Output extension {ext} does not support PCM audio, and a "
390                    "default audio codec could not be determined. Please choose a "
391                    "suitable audio codec with the -c:a option."
392                )
393
394        self.media_files.append(MediaFile(self, input_file, output_file))
395        self.file_count += 1

397    @staticmethod
398    def validate_input_files(input_files: list[str]) -> list[str]:
399        """
400        Validate all input files before processing.
401
402        This method checks that each input file exists, is readable, and contains
403        at least one audio stream. All files are validated upfront so that users
404        can fix all issues before rerunning the batch.
405
406        Args:
407            input_files: List of input file paths to validate
408
409        Returns:
410            list: List of error messages for invalid files. Empty if all files are valid.
411        """
412        errors = []
413        for input_file in input_files:
414            is_valid, error_msg = validate_input_file(input_file)
415            if not is_valid and error_msg:
416                errors.append(error_msg)
417        return errors
418
419    @staticmethod
420    def validate_output_files(input_files: list[str], output_files: list[str]) -> None:
421        """Reject duplicate destinations and outputs that overwrite another input.
422
423        Resolve symlinks and existing hard links, while allowing each file to be
424        normalized in place and multiple outputs to the null device.
425        """
426
427        def path_keys(path: str) -> list[str | tuple[int, int]]:
428            keys: list[str | tuple[int, int]] = [
429                os.path.normcase(os.path.realpath(path))
430            ]
431            if os.path.exists(path):
432                stat = os.stat(path)
433                keys.append((stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino))
434            return keys
435
436        input_owners: dict[str | tuple[int, int], set[int]] = {}
437        for index, path in enumerate(input_files):
438            for key in path_keys(path):
439                input_owners.setdefault(key, set()).add(index)
440
441        output_owners: dict[str | tuple[int, int], str] = {}
442        for index, path in enumerate(output_files):
443            if os.path.realpath(path) == os.path.realpath(os.devnull):
444                continue
445            for key in path_keys(path):
446                if key in output_owners:
447                    raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
448                        f"Output collision: '{path}' and '{output_owners[key]}' "
449                        "refer to the same destination. Specify distinct output paths."
450                    )
451                if input_owners.get(key, set()) - {index}:
452                    raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
453                        f"Output '{path}' would overwrite another input file. "
454                        "Specify a different output path."
455                    )
456                output_owners[key] = path
457
458    def _calculate_batch_reference(self) -> float | None:
459        """
460        Calculate a shared reference from the selected streams' measurements.
461
462        Peak mode uses the highest sample peak. RMS mode uses the average RMS,
463        with gain capped by the highest sample peak. EBU uses average LUFS.
464
465        Returns:
466            float | None: The batch reference loudness value, or None if no measurements found.
467
468        Note:
469            RMS and EBU averages weight each selected stream equally.
470        """
471        measurements: list[float] = []
472        peaks: list[float] = []
473
474        for media_file in self.media_files:
475            if media_file.status == "error":
476                continue
477            for stream in media_file._get_streams_to_normalize():
478                peak = stream.loudness_statistics.get("max")
479                if peak is not None and math.isfinite(peak):
480                    peaks.append(float(peak))
481                if self.normalization_type == "ebu":
482                    # Get EBU integrated loudness from first pass
483                    ebu_stats = stream.loudness_statistics.get("ebu_pass1")
484                    if ebu_stats and "input_i" in ebu_stats:
485                        measurements.append(float(ebu_stats["input_i"]))
486                elif self.normalization_type == "rms":
487                    # Get RMS mean value
488                    mean = stream.loudness_statistics.get("mean")
489                    if mean is not None:
490                        measurements.append(float(mean))
491                elif self.normalization_type == "peak":
492                    # Get peak max value
493                    max_val = stream.loudness_statistics.get("max")
494                    if max_val is not None:
495                        measurements.append(float(max_val))
496
497        measurements = [value for value in measurements if math.isfinite(value)]
498        if not measurements:
499            _logger.warning(
500                "No loudness measurements found for batch reference calculation. "
501                "Batch mode will not be applied."
502            )
503            return None
504
505        # Peak mode targets the loudest sample in the album. RMS mode targets
506        # the average level, but limits the shared gain to available headroom.
507        batch_reference = (
508            max(measurements)
509            if self.normalization_type == "peak"
510            else sum(measurements) / len(measurements)
511        )
512        if self.normalization_type == "rms" and peaks:
513            safe_reference = self.target_level + max(peaks)
514            if safe_reference > batch_reference:
515                _logger.warning(
516                    "Reducing album gain to avoid sample clipping; "
517                    "the requested RMS target will not be reached."
518                )
519                batch_reference = safe_reference
520        if self.lower_only and self.normalization_type in ("peak", "rms"):
521            batch_reference = max(batch_reference, self.target_level)
522        _logger.debug(f"Batch mode: Measurements for batch reference: {measurements}")
523        _logger.info(
524            f"Batch mode: Calculated reference loudness = {batch_reference:.2f} "
525            f"({self.normalization_type.upper()}, based on {len(measurements)} stream(s))"
526        )
527
528        return batch_reference
529
530    def _iter_media_files(self, description: str) -> Iterator[tuple[int, MediaFile]]:
531        """
532        Iterate over all media files while updating the overall progress bar.
533
534        Args:
535            description (str): Label of the overall progress bar
536
537        Yields:
538            tuple[int, MediaFile]: The index and the media file
539        """
540        display = self.progress_display
541        display.start_overall(description, self.file_count)
542        for index, media_file in enumerate(self.media_files):
543            display.set_current(display_name(media_file.input_file))
544            yield index, media_file
545            display.advance_overall()
546        display.set_current(None)
547
548    def run_normalization(self) -> None:
549        """
550        Run the normalization procedures.
551
552        In batch mode, all files are analyzed first (first pass), then a batch reference
553        loudness is calculated, and finally all files are normalized (second pass) with
554        adjustments relative to the batch reference to preserve relative loudness.
555
556        In non-batch mode, each file is processed completely (both passes) before
557        moving to the next file.
558        """
559        if (
560            self.verify
561            and not self.dry_run
562            and any(
563                os.path.realpath(file.output_file) == os.path.realpath(os.devnull)
564                for file in self.media_files
565            )
566        ):
567            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
568                "--verify requires an output file, not the null device"
569            )
570        if not self.replaygain:
571            self.validate_output_files(
572                [media_file.input_file for media_file in self.media_files],
573                [media_file.output_file for media_file in self.media_files],
574            )
575        with ProgressDisplay(enabled=self.progress) as display:
576            self.progress_display = display
577            try:
578                self._process_media_files()
579            finally:
580                self.progress_display = ProgressDisplay(enabled=False)
581
582        if self.print_stats:
583            json.dump(
584                list(
585                    chain.from_iterable(
586                        media_file.get_stats() for media_file in self.media_files
587                    )
588                ),
589                sys.stdout,
590                indent=4,
591            )
592            print()
593
594        if self.print_summary:
595            console = get_console()
596            if console.is_terminal:
597                console.print(self.summary_renderable())
598            else:
599                print(self.format_summary(), file=sys.stderr)
600
601    def _process_media_files(self) -> None:
602        """Run both passes for all media files, in batch or per-file mode."""
603        if self.batch:
604            # Batch mode: analyze all files first, then normalize with relative adjustments
605            _logger.info(
606                f"Batch mode enabled: processing {self.file_count} file(s) while preserving relative loudness"
607            )
608
609            # Recommend RMS/Peak for album normalization instead of EBU
610            if self.normalization_type == "ebu":
611                _logger.warning(
612                    "Using EBU R128 normalization with --batch. For true album normalization where "
613                    "all tracks are shifted by the same amount, consider using --normalization-type rms "
614                    "or --normalization-type peak instead. EBU normalization applies different processing "
615                    "to each track based on its loudness characteristics, which may alter relative levels "
616                    "slightly due to psychoacoustic adjustments."
617                )
618
619            # Warn if using dynamic EBU mode with batch
620            if self.dynamic and self.normalization_type == "ebu":
621                _logger.warning(
622                    "ffmpeg uses dynamic EBU normalization. This may change relative "
623                    "loudness within a file. Use linear mode for true album normalization, or "
624                    "switch to --normalization-type peak or --normalization-type rms instead. "
625                    "To force linear mode, use --keep-lra-above-loudness-range-target or "
626                    "--keep-loudness-range-target."
627                )
628
629            # Phase 1: Run first pass on all files to collect measurements
630            _logger.info("Phase 1: Analyzing all files...")
631            for index, media_file in self._iter_media_files("Analysis"):
632                _logger.info(
633                    f"Analyzing file {media_file} ({index + 1} of {self.file_count})"
634                )
635
636                try:
637                    # Only run first pass if not in dynamic EBU mode
638                    if not (self.dynamic and self.normalization_type == "ebu"):
639                        media_file._first_pass()
640                    else:
641                        _logger.debug(
642                            "Dynamic EBU mode: First pass skipped for this file."
643                        )
644                except Exception as e:
645                    self._record_failure(media_file, e, "analyzing")
646                    continue
647
648            # Phase 2: Calculate batch reference loudness
649            batch_reference = self._calculate_batch_reference()
650
651            # Phase 3: Run second pass on all files with batch reference
652            _logger.info("Phase 2: Normalizing all files...")
653            for index, media_file in self._iter_media_files("Normalization"):
654                # Skip files that already failed during analysis
655                if media_file.status == "error":
656                    _logger.debug(f"Skipping {media_file} because its analysis failed")
657                    continue
658
659                _logger.info(
660                    f"Normalizing file {media_file} ({index + 1} of {self.file_count})"
661                )
662
663                try:
664                    media_file.run_normalization(batch_reference=batch_reference)
665                    if self.verify and not self.dry_run:
666                        media_file.verify_output()
667                except Exception as e:
668                    self._record_failure(media_file, e, "processing")
669                    continue
670        else:
671            # Non-batch mode: process each file completely before moving to the next
672            for index, media_file in self._iter_media_files("Files"):
673                _logger.info(
674                    f"Normalizing file {media_file} ({index + 1} of {self.file_count})"
675                )
676
677                try:
678                    media_file.run_normalization()
679                    if self.verify and not self.dry_run:
680                        media_file.verify_output()
681                except Exception as e:
682                    self._record_failure(media_file, e, "processing")
683                    continue
684
685    @staticmethod
686    def _record_failure(media_file: MediaFile, error: Exception, action: str) -> None:
687        """
688        Mark a media file as failed and log a short description of the error.
689
690        The full error (e.g. the complete ffmpeg output) is only logged in
691        debug mode.
692
693        Args:
694            media_file (MediaFile): The file that failed
695            error (Exception): The error
696            action (str): What was being done, e.g. "processing"
697        """
698        media_file.status = "error"
699        media_file.error = describe_error(error)
700        _logger.debug(f"Full error for {media_file.input_file}: {error}", exc_info=True)
701        _logger.error(f"Error {action} input file {media_file}: {media_file.error}")
702
703    def get_summary(self) -> list[SummaryRow]:
704        """
705        Return the before/after summary for all audio streams of all files.
706
707        Each entry contains the input level, output level, output peak and the
708        applied gain in dB. The level is the integrated loudness for EBU, the
709        RMS level for RMS, and the peak level for peak normalization. The
710        output peak is the true peak for EBU and the sample peak otherwise.
711        Values that are not available are None.
712
713        Returns:
714            list[SummaryRow]: One summary entry per audio stream
715        """
716        return list(
717            chain.from_iterable(
718                media_file.get_summary() for media_file in self.media_files
719            )
720        )
721
722    def _summary_parts(
723        self,
724    ) -> tuple[str, list[str], list[list[str]], list[tuple[str, bool]], list[str]]:
725        """
726        Collect the pieces of the before/after summary.
727
728        Returns:
729            tuple: The header, the column headings, the table rows, the
730                verification lines (text and whether the check passed), and
731                additional notes
732        """
733        if self.normalization_type == "ebu":
734            header = (
735                f"EBU R128 normalization, target: {self.target_level:.1f} LUFS, "
736                f"true peak: {self.true_peak:.1f} dBTP"
737            )
738            if self.dynamic:
739                header += ", dynamic mode"
740            columns = ["Input (LUFS)", "Output (LUFS)", "True peak (dBTP)", "Gain (dB)"]
741        elif self.normalization_type == "rms":
742            header = f"RMS normalization, target: {self.target_level:.1f} dBFS"
743            columns = [
744                "Input RMS (dBFS)",
745                "Output RMS (dBFS)",
746                "Peak (dBFS)",
747                "Gain (dB)",
748            ]
749        else:
750            header = f"Peak normalization, target: {self.target_level:.1f} dBFS"
751            columns = ["Input peak (dBFS)", "Output peak (dBFS)", "Gain (dB)"]
752
753        if self.batch:
754            header += ", batch mode (relative loudness preserved)"
755        if self.dry_run:
756            header += ", dry run"
757
758        def fmt(value: float | None, signed: bool = False) -> str:
759            if value is None:
760                return "-"
761            return f"{value:+.1f}" if signed else f"{value:.1f}"
762
763        rows = self.get_summary()
764        table: list[list[str]] = []
765        for row in rows:
766            values = [fmt(row["input_level"]), fmt(row["output_level"])]
767            if self.normalization_type != "peak":
768                values.append(fmt(row["output_peak"]))
769            values.append(fmt(row["gain"], signed=True))
770            table.append(
771                [row["input_file"], str(row["stream_id"]), *values, row["status"]]
772            )
773
774        verifications: list[tuple[str, bool]] = []
775        notes: list[str] = []
776        verified = [row for row in rows if "verification" in row]
777        if verified:
778            level_unit = "LUFS" if self.normalization_type == "ebu" else "dBFS"
779            peak_unit = "dBTP" if self.normalization_type == "ebu" else "dBFS"
780            for row in verified:
781                result = row["verification"]
782                outcome = "passed" if result["passed"] else "FAILED"
783                verifications.append(
784                    (
785                        f"{row['output_file']} stream {result['output_stream_id']}: "
786                        f"level {fmt(result['output_level'])} {level_unit}, "
787                        f"peak {fmt(result['output_peak'])} {peak_unit}, {outcome}",
788                        result["passed"],
789                    )
790                )
791        elif self.verify and self.dry_run:
792            notes.append("Encoded-output verification skipped: dry run.")
793
794        return (
795            header,
796            ["File", "Stream", *columns, "Status"],
797            table,
798            verifications,
799            notes,
800        )
801
802    _SUMMARY_FOOTNOTE = (
803        "Output values above: loudnorm filter statistics for EBU; "
804        "calculated from applied gain for RMS/peak; input levels for skipped files."
805    )
806
807    def format_summary(self) -> str:
808        """
809        Return the before/after summary as a human-readable table.
810
811        Returns:
812            str: The formatted table, including a header line with the target
813        """
814        header, headings, table, verifications, notes = self._summary_parts()
815        if not table:
816            return f"Summary ({header}): no files processed"
817
818        widths = [
819            max(len(headings[i]), *(len(line[i]) for line in table))
820            for i in range(len(headings))
821        ]
822
823        def fmt_line(cells: list[str]) -> str:
824            # Left-align the file name and status, right-align everything else
825            parts = [
826                cell.ljust(widths[i])
827                if i in (0, len(cells) - 1)
828                else cell.rjust(widths[i])
829                for i, cell in enumerate(cells)
830            ]
831            return "  ".join(parts).rstrip()
832
833        lines = [f"Summary ({header}):", "", fmt_line(headings)]
834        lines.append(fmt_line(["-" * w for w in widths]))
835        lines.extend(fmt_line(line) for line in table)
836        lines.append("\n" + self._SUMMARY_FOOTNOTE)
837        if verifications:
838            lines.append("\nEncoded-output verification (measured after encoding):")
839            lines.extend(text for text, _ in verifications)
840        for note in notes:
841            lines.append("\n" + note)
842        return "\n".join(lines)
843
844    def summary_renderable(self) -> RenderableType:
845        """
846        Return the before/after summary as a rich renderable for terminals.
847
848        Returns:
849            RenderableType: A table with the same content as `format_summary()`
850        """
851        header, headings, table, verifications, notes = self._summary_parts()
852        if not table:
853            return Text(f"Summary ({header}): no files processed")
854
855        status_styles = {"normalized": "status.ok", "skipped": "status.skipped"}
856        summary = Table(
857            title=f"Summary ({header})",
858            title_justify="left",
859            title_style="bold",
860            caption=self._SUMMARY_FOOTNOTE,
861            caption_justify="left",
862            caption_style="dim",
863            header_style="bold",
864            box=box.SIMPLE_HEAD,
865        )
866        last = len(headings) - 1
867        for i, heading in enumerate(headings):
868            summary.add_column(
869                heading,
870                justify="left" if i in (0, last) else "right",
871                overflow="fold",
872                no_wrap=i != 0,
873            )
874        for line in table:
875            status = line[-1]
876            summary.add_row(
877                *line[:-1],
878                Text(status, style=status_styles.get(status, "status.error")),
879            )
880
881        parts: list[RenderableType] = [summary]
882        if verifications:
883            parts.append(
884                Text(
885                    "Encoded-output verification (measured after encoding):",
886                    style="bold",
887                )
888            )
889            for text, passed in verifications:
890                parts.append(
891                    Text(
892                        f"  {'✔' if passed else '✘'} {text}",
893                        style="status.ok" if passed else "status.error",
894                    )
895                )
896        parts.extend(Text(note, style="dim") for note in notes)
897        return Group(*parts)

ffmpeg-normalize class.

Arguments:
  • normalization_type (str, optional): Normalization type. Defaults to "ebu".
  • target_level (float, optional): Target level. Defaults to -23.0.
  • print_stats (bool, optional): Print loudnorm stats. Defaults to False.
  • print_summary (bool, optional): Print a before/after summary table to stderr after processing. Defaults to False.
  • threshold (float, optional): When set to a positive value, skip normalization when the input is already within this many dB/LU of the target level, copying it through unchanged. Defaults to 0 (disabled, always normalize).
  • loudness_range_target (float, optional): Loudness range target. Defaults to 7.0.
  • keep_loudness_range_target (bool, optional): Keep loudness range target. Defaults to False.
  • keep_lra_above_loudness_range_target (bool, optional): Keep input loudness range above loudness range target. Defaults to False.
  • true_peak (float, optional): True peak. Defaults to -2.0.
  • offset (float, optional): Offset. Defaults to 0.0.
  • lower_only (bool, optional): Whether the audio should not increase in loudness. Defaults to False.
  • auto_lower_loudness_target (bool, optional): Automatically lower EBU Integrated Loudness Target.
  • dual_mono (bool, optional): Dual mono. Defaults to False.
  • dynamic (bool, optional): Use dynamic EBU R128 normalization. This is a one-pass algorithm and skips the initial media scan. Defaults to False.
  • audio_codec (str, optional): Audio codec. Defaults to "pcm_s16le".
  • audio_bitrate (float, optional): Audio bitrate. Defaults to None.
  • sample_rate (int, optional): Sample rate. Defaults to None.
  • audio_channels (int | None, optional): Audio channels. Defaults to None.
  • keep_original_audio (bool, optional): Keep original audio. Defaults to False.
  • pre_filter (str, optional): Pre filter. Defaults to None.
  • post_filter (str, optional): Post filter. Defaults to None.
  • video_codec (str, optional): Video codec. Defaults to "copy".
  • video_disable (bool, optional): Disable video. Defaults to False.
  • subtitle_disable (bool, optional): Disable subtitles. Defaults to False.
  • metadata_disable (bool, optional): Disable metadata. Defaults to False.
  • chapters_disable (bool, optional): Disable chapters. Defaults to False.
  • write_encoder_settings (bool, optional): Write the effective encoder settings (codec, bitrate, sample rate, channels and the normalization filter including the measured loudnorm values) as an ENCODER_SETTINGS tag on each normalized audio stream. Defaults to False.
  • extra_input_options (list, optional): Extra input options. Defaults to None.
  • extra_output_options (list, optional): Extra output options. Defaults to None.
  • output_format (str, optional): Output format. Defaults to None.
  • extension (str, optional): Output file extension to use for output files that were not explicitly specified. Defaults to "mkv".
  • dry_run (bool, optional): Dry run. Defaults to False.
  • debug (bool, optional): Debug. Defaults to False.
  • progress (bool, optional): Progress. Defaults to False.
  • replaygain (bool, optional): Write ReplayGain tags without normalizing. Defaults to False.
  • batch (bool, optional): Preserve relative loudness between files (album mode). Defaults to False.
  • audio_streams (list[int] | None, optional): List of audio stream indices to normalize. Defaults to None (all streams).
  • audio_default_only (bool, optional): Only normalize audio streams with default disposition. Defaults to False.
  • keep_other_audio (bool, optional): Keep non-selected audio streams in output (copy without normalization). Defaults to False.
  • keep_mtime (bool, optional): Copy the input file's modification time to the output file. Defaults to False.
  • keep_bit_depth (bool, optional): Carry the detected input bit depth through to the output encoder. Defaults to True.
  • verify (bool, optional): Measure the encoded output and check its effective target and peak ceiling. Defaults to False. Not available with ReplayGain; skipped during dry runs.
  • verify_loudness_tolerance (float, optional): Allowed level deviation in dB/LU. Defaults to 0.5.
  • verify_peak_tolerance (float, optional): Allowed peak overshoot in dB. Defaults to 0.1.
Raises:
  • FFmpegNormalizeError: If the ffmpeg executable is not found or does not support the loudnorm filter.

320            math.isfinite(value)
321            for value in (self.verify_loudness_tolerance, self.verify_peak_tolerance)
322        ):
323            raise FFmpegNormalizeError("Verification tolerances must be finite")
324        if verify and replaygain:
325            raise FFmpegNormalizeError("--verify cannot be combined with --replaygain")
326
327        if self.output_format in PCM_INCOMPATIBLE_FORMATS:
328            if self.audio_codec is not None and "pcm" in self.audio_codec:
329                raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
330                    f"Output format {self.output_format} does not support PCM audio. "
331                    "Please choose a suitable audio codec with the -c:a option."
332                )
333            if (
334                self.audio_codec is None
335                and get_muxer_default_audio_encoder(self.output_format) is None
336            ):
337                raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
338                    f"Output format {self.output_format} does not support PCM audio, "
339                    "and a default audio codec could not be determined. Please choose "
340                    "a suitable audio codec with the -c:a option."
341                )
342
343        # replaygain only works for EBU for now
344        if self.replaygain and self.normalization_type != "ebu":
345            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
346                "ReplayGain only works for EBU normalization type for now."
347            )
348
349        # Validate stream selection options
350        if self.audio_streams is not None and self.audio_default_only:
351            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
352                "Cannot use both audio_streams and audio_default_only together."
353            )
354
355        if self.keep_other_audio and self.keep_original_audio:
356            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
357                "Cannot use both --keep-other-audio and --keep-original-audio together. "
358                "Use --keep-original-audio to keep all original streams alongside normalized ones, "
359                "or --keep-other-audio to keep only non-selected streams as passthrough."
360            )
361
362        self.stats: list[LoudnessStatisticsWithMetadata] = []
363        self.media_files: list[MediaFile] = []
364        self.file_count = 0

399        """
400        Validate all input files before processing.

@staticmethod
def validate_output_files(input_files: list[str], output_files: list[str]) -> None: 
419    @staticmethod
420    def validate_output_files(input_files: list[str], output_files: list[str]) -> None:
421        """Reject duplicate destinations and outputs that overwrite another input.
422
423        Resolve symlinks and existing hard links, while allowing each file to be
424        normalized in place and multiple outputs to the null device.
425        """
426
427        def path_keys(path: str) -> list[str | tuple[int, int]]:
428            keys: list[str | tuple[int, int]] = [
429                os.path.normcase(os.path.realpath(path))
430            ]
431            if os.path.exists(path):
432                stat = os.stat(path)
433                keys.append((stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino))
434            return keys
435
436        input_owners: dict[str | tuple[int, int], set[int]] = {}
437        for index, path in enumerate(input_files):
438            for key in path_keys(path):
439                input_owners.setdefault(key, set()).add(index)
440
441        output_owners: dict[str | tuple[int, int], str] = {}
442        for index, path in enumerate(output_files):
443            if os.path.realpath(path) == os.path.realpath(os.devnull):
444                continue
445            for key in path_keys(path):
446                if key in output_owners:
447                    raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
448                        f"Output collision: '{path}' and '{output_owners[key]}' "
449                        "refer to the same destination. Specify distinct output paths."
450                    )
451                if input_owners.get(key, set()) - {index}:
452                    raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
453                        f"Output '{path}' would overwrite another input file. "
454                        "Specify a different output path."
455                    )
456                output_owners[key] = path

def run_normalization(self) -> None: 
548    def run_normalization(self) -> None:
549        """
550        Run the normalization procedures.
551
552        In batch mode, all files are analyzed first (first pass), then a batch reference
553        loudness is calculated, and finally all files are normalized (second pass) with
554        adjustments relative to the batch reference to preserve relative loudness.
555
556        In non-batch mode, each file is processed completely (both passes) before
557        moving to the next file.
558        """
559        if (
560            self.verify
561            and not self.dry_run
562            and any(
563                os.path.realpath(file.output_file) == os.path.realpath(os.devnull)
564                for file in self.media_files
565            )
566        ):
567            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
568                "--verify requires an output file, not the null device"
569            )
570        if not self.replaygain:
571            self.validate_output_files(
572                [media_file.input_file for media_file in self.media_files],
573                [media_file.output_file for media_file in self.media_files],
574            )
575        with ProgressDisplay(enabled=self.progress) as display:
576            self.progress_display = display
577            try:
578                self._process_media_files()
579            finally:
580                self.progress_display = ProgressDisplay(enabled=False)
581
582        if self.print_stats:
583            json.dump(
584                list(
585                    chain.from_iterable(
586                        media_file.get_stats() for media_file in self.media_files
587                    )
588                ),
589                sys.stdout,
590                indent=4,
591            )
592            print()
593
594        if self.print_summary:
595            console = get_console()
596            if console.is_terminal:
597                console.print(self.summary_renderable())
598            else:
599                print(self.format_summary(), file=sys.stderr)

Run the normalization procedures.

In batch mode, all files are analyzed first (first pass), then a batch reference loudness is calculated, and finally all files are normalized (second pass) with adjustments relative to the batch reference to preserve relative loudness.

In non-batch mode, each file is processed completely (both passes) before moving to the next file.

def get_summary(self) -> list[ffmpeg_normalize._streams.SummaryRow]: 
703    def get_summary(self) -> list[SummaryRow]:
704        """
705        Return the before/after summary for all audio streams of all files.
706
707        Each entry contains the input level, output level, output peak and the
708        applied gain in dB. The level is the integrated loudness for EBU, the
709        RMS level for RMS, and the peak level for peak normalization. The
710        output peak is the true peak for EBU and the sample peak otherwise.
711        Values that are not available are None.
712
713        Returns:
714            list[SummaryRow]: One summary entry per audio stream
715        """
716        return list(
717            chain.from_iterable(
718                media_file.get_summary() for media_file in self.media_files
719            )
720        )

def format_summary(self) -> str: 
807    def format_summary(self) -> str:
808        """
809        Return the before/after summary as a human-readable table.
810
811        Returns:
812            str: The formatted table, including a header line with the target
813        """
814        header, headings, table, verifications, notes = self._summary_parts()
815        if not table:
816            return f"Summary ({header}): no files processed"
817
818        widths = [
819            max(len(headings[i]), *(len(line[i]) for line in table))
820            for i in range(len(headings))
821        ]
822
823        def fmt_line(cells: list[str]) -> str:
824            # Left-align the file name and status, right-align everything else
825            parts = [
826                cell.ljust(widths[i])
827                if i in (0, len(cells) - 1)
828                else cell.rjust(widths[i])
829                for i, cell in enumerate(cells)
830            ]
831            return "  ".join(parts).rstrip()
832
833        lines = [f"Summary ({header}):", "", fmt_line(headings)]
834        lines.append(fmt_line(["-" * w for w in widths]))
835        lines.extend(fmt_line(line) for line in table)
836        lines.append("\n" + self._SUMMARY_FOOTNOTE)
837        if verifications:
838            lines.append("\nEncoded-output verification (measured after encoding):")
839            lines.extend(text for text, _ in verifications)
840        for note in notes:
841            lines.append("\n" + note)
842        return "\n".join(lines)

def summary_renderable(self) -> rich.console.ConsoleRenderable | rich.console.RichCast | str: 
844    def summary_renderable(self) -> RenderableType:
845        """
846        Return the before/after summary as a rich renderable for terminals.
847
848        Returns:
849            RenderableType: A table with the same content as `format_summary()`
850        """
851        header, headings, table, verifications, notes = self._summary_parts()
852        if not table:
853            return Text(f"Summary ({header}): no files processed")
854
855        status_styles = {"normalized": "status.ok", "skipped": "status.skipped"}
856        summary = Table(
857            title=f"Summary ({header})",
858            title_justify="left",
859            title_style="bold",
860            caption=self._SUMMARY_FOOTNOTE,
861            caption_justify="left",
862            caption_style="dim",
863            header_style="bold",
864            box=box.SIMPLE_HEAD,
865        )
866        last = len(headings) - 1
867        for i, heading in enumerate(headings):
868            summary.add_column(
869                heading,
870                justify="left" if i in (0, last) else "right",
871                overflow="fold",
872                no_wrap=i != 0,
873            )
874        for line in table:
875            status = line[-1]
876            summary.add_row(
877                *line[:-1],
878                Text(status, style=status_styles.get(status, "status.error")),
879            )
880
881        parts: list[RenderableType] = [summary]
882        if verifications:
883            parts.append(
884                Text(
885                    "Encoded-output verification (measured after encoding):",
886                    style="bold",
887                )
888            )
889            for text, passed in verifications:
890                parts.append(
891                    Text(
892                        f"  {'✔' if passed else '✘'} {text}",
893                        style="status.ok" if passed else "status.error",
894                    )
895                )
896        parts.extend(Text(note, style="dim") for note in notes)
897        return Group(*parts)

Return the before/after summary as a rich renderable for terminals.

Returns:

RenderableType: A table with the same content as format_summary()
