class MediaFile: 
  63class MediaFile:
  64    """
  65    Class that holds a file, its streams and adjustments
  66    """
  67
  68    def __init__(
  69        self, ffmpeg_normalize: FFmpegNormalize, input_file: str, output_file: str
  70    ):
  71        """
  72        Initialize a media file for later normalization by parsing the streams.
  73
  74        Args:
  75            ffmpeg_normalize (FFmpegNormalize): reference to overall settings
  76            input_file (str): Path to input file
  77            output_file (str): Path to output file
  78        """
  79        self.ffmpeg_normalize = ffmpeg_normalize
  80        self.skip = False
  81        # Per-file outcome, reported in the --print-stats output: "normalized"
  82        # (default), "skipped" (already within threshold of target), or "error".
  83        # "error" is set by FFmpegNormalize.run_normalization when processing
  84        # fails; on failure, self.error holds the error message.
  85        self.status: str = "normalized"
  86        self.error: str | None = None
  87        self.input_file = input_file
  88        self.output_file = output_file
  89        current_ext = os.path.splitext(output_file)[1][1:]
  90        # we need to check if it's empty, e.g. /dev/null or NUL
  91        if current_ext == "" or self.output_file == os.devnull:
  92            _logger.debug(
  93                f"Current extension is unset, or output file is a null device, using extension: {self.ffmpeg_normalize.extension}"
  94            )
  95            self.output_ext = self.ffmpeg_normalize.extension
  96        else:
  97            _logger.debug(
  98                f"Current extension is set from output file, using extension: {current_ext}"
  99            )
 100            self.output_ext = current_ext
 101        self.streams: StreamDict = {"audio": {}, "video": {}, "subtitle": {}}
 102        self.temp_file: Union[str, None] = None
 103        self.batch_reference: float | None = None
 104        # Second-pass filter chain per normalized audio stream, keyed by stream
 105        # id. Populated by _get_audio_filter_cmd() and reused by
 106        # _get_encoder_settings() so the normalization filter is not built twice.
 107        self._stream_filter_chains: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
 108        # Input (access, modification) times captured before processing, used
 109        # when the keep_mtime option is enabled.
 110        self.input_timestamps: tuple[float, float] | None = None
 111
 112        self.parse_streams()
 113
 114    def _stream_ids(self) -> list[int]:
 115        """
 116        Get all stream IDs of this file.
 117
 118        Returns:
 119            list: List of stream IDs
 120        """
 121        return (
 122            list(self.streams["audio"].keys())
 123            + list(self.streams["video"].keys())
 124            + list(self.streams["subtitle"].keys())
 125        )
 126
 127    def __repr__(self) -> str:
 128        return os.path.basename(self.input_file)
 129
 130    def parse_streams(self) -> None:
 131        """
 132        Try to parse all input streams from file and set them in self.streams.
 133
 134        Raises:
 135            FFmpegNormalizeError: If no audio streams are found
 136        """
 137        _logger.debug(f"Parsing streams of {self.input_file}")
 138
 139        cmd = [
 140            self.ffmpeg_normalize.ffmpeg_exe,
 141            "-i",
 142            self.input_file,
 143            "-c",
 144            "copy",
 145            "-t",
 146            "0",
 147            "-map",
 148            "0",
 149            "-f",
 150            "null",
 151            os.devnull,
 152        ]
 153
 154        output = CommandRunner().run_command(cmd).get_output()
 155
 156        _logger.debug("Stream parsing command output:")
 157        _logger.debug(output)
 158
 159        output_lines = [line.strip() for line in output.split("\n")]
 160
 161        # First pass: parse disposition flags for each stream
 162        stream_dispositions: dict[int, bool] = {}
 163
 164        for line in output_lines:
 165            if line.startswith("Stream"):
 166                if stream_id_match := re.search(r"#0:([\d]+)", line):
 167                    stream_id = int(stream_id_match.group(1))
 168                    # Check if (default) appears on the Stream line
 169                    is_default = "(default)" in line
 170                    stream_dispositions[stream_id] = is_default
 171
 172        # Second pass: parse stream information
 173        duration = None
 174        for line in output_lines:
 175            if "Duration" in line:
 176                if duration_search := DUR_REGEX.search(line):
 177                    duration = _to_ms(**duration_search.groupdict()) / 1000
 178                    _logger.debug(f"Found duration: {duration} s")
 179                else:
 180                    _logger.warning("Could not extract duration from input file!")
 181
 182            if not line.startswith("Stream"):
 183                continue
 184
 185            if stream_id_match := re.search(r"#0:([\d]+)", line):
 186                stream_id = int(stream_id_match.group(1))
 187                if stream_id in self._stream_ids():
 188                    continue
 189            else:
 190                continue
 191
 192            is_default = stream_dispositions.get(stream_id, False)
 193
 194            if "Audio" in line:
 195                _logger.debug(
 196                    f"Found audio stream at index {stream_id} (default: {is_default})"
 197                )
 198                sample_rate_match = re.search(r"(\d+) Hz", line)
 199                sample_rate = (
 200                    int(sample_rate_match.group(1)) if sample_rate_match else None
 201                )
 202                bit_depth_match = re.search(r"([sfu])(\d+)(p|le|be)?", line)
 203                bit_depth = int(bit_depth_match.group(2)) if bit_depth_match else None
 204                is_float = bit_depth_match.group(1) == "f" if bit_depth_match else False
 205                self.streams["audio"][stream_id] = AudioStream(
 206                    self.ffmpeg_normalize,
 207                    self,
 208                    stream_id,
 209                    sample_rate,
 210                    bit_depth,
 211                    duration,
 212                    is_default,
 213                    is_float,
 214                )
 215
 216            elif "Video" in line:
 217                _logger.debug(f"Found video stream at index {stream_id}")
 218                self.streams["video"][stream_id] = VideoStream(
 219                    self.ffmpeg_normalize, self, stream_id
 220                )
 221
 222            elif "Subtitle" in line:
 223                _logger.debug(f"Found subtitle stream at index {stream_id}")
 224                self.streams["subtitle"][stream_id] = SubtitleStream(
 225                    self.ffmpeg_normalize, self, stream_id
 226                )
 227
 228        if not self.streams["audio"]:
 229            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
 230                f"Input file {self.input_file} does not contain any audio streams"
 231            )
 232
 233        if (
 234            self.output_ext.lower() in ONE_STREAM
 235            and len(self.streams["audio"].values()) > 1
 236        ):
 237            _logger.warning(
 238                "Output file only supports one stream. Keeping only first audio stream."
 239            )
 240            first_stream = list(self.streams["audio"].values())[0]
 241            self.streams["audio"] = {first_stream.stream_id: first_stream}
 242            self.streams["video"] = {}
 243            self.streams["subtitle"] = {}
 244
 245    def _get_streams_to_normalize(self) -> list[AudioStream]:
 246        """
 247        Determine which audio streams to normalize based on configuration.
 248
 249        Returns:
 250            list[AudioStream]: List of audio streams to normalize
 251        """
 252        all_audio_streams = list(self.streams["audio"].values())
 253
 254        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_streams is not None:
 255            # User specified specific stream indices
 256            selected_streams = [
 257                stream
 258                for stream in all_audio_streams
 259                if stream.stream_id in self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_streams
 260            ]
 261            if not selected_streams:
 262                _logger.warning(
 263                    f"No audio streams found matching indices {self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_streams}. "
 264                    f"Available streams: {[s.stream_id for s in all_audio_streams]}"
 265                )
 266            else:
 267                _logger.info(
 268                    f"Normalizing selected audio streams: {[s.stream_id for s in selected_streams]}"
 269                )
 270            return selected_streams
 271
 272        elif self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_default_only:
 273            # Only normalize streams with default disposition
 274            default_streams = [
 275                stream for stream in all_audio_streams if stream.is_default
 276            ]
 277            if not default_streams:
 278                _logger.warning(
 279                    "No audio streams with 'default' disposition found. "
 280                    f"Available streams: {[s.stream_id for s in all_audio_streams]}"
 281                )
 282            else:
 283                _logger.info(
 284                    f"Normalizing default audio streams: {[s.stream_id for s in default_streams]}"
 285                )
 286            return default_streams
 287
 288        else:
 289            # Normalize all streams (default behavior)
 290            return all_audio_streams
 291
 292    def run_normalization(self, batch_reference: float | None = None) -> None:
 293        """
 294        Run the normalization process for this file.
 295
 296        Args:
 297            batch_reference (float | None, optional): Reference loudness for batch mode.
 298                If provided, the first pass is skipped (assumed already done) and this
 299                reference is used to calculate relative adjustments. Defaults to None.
 300        """
 301        _logger.debug(f"Running normalization for {self.input_file}")
 302
 303        # Store batch reference for use in second pass
 304        self.batch_reference = batch_reference
 305
 306        # Capture the input file's timestamps before processing, since an
 307        # in-place overwrite would otherwise lose the original modification time.
 308        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_mtime:
 309            try:
 310                stat = os.stat(self.input_file)
 311                self.input_timestamps = (stat.st_atime, stat.st_mtime)
 312            except OSError as e:
 313                _logger.warning(
 314                    f"Could not read timestamps from {self.input_file}: {e}"
 315                )
 316
 317        # run the first pass to get loudness stats, unless in dynamic EBU mode or batch mode
 318        # (in batch mode, first pass is already done in FFmpegNormalize.run_normalization)
 319        if batch_reference is None:
 320            if not (
 321                self.ffmpeg_normalize.dynamic
 322                and self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type == "ebu"
 323            ):
 324                self._first_pass()
 325            else:
 326                _logger.debug(
 327                    "Dynamic EBU mode: First pass will not run, as it is not needed."
 328                )
 329        else:
 330            _logger.debug(
 331                f"Batch mode: Skipping first pass (already completed), using batch reference = {batch_reference:.2f}"
 332            )
 333
 334        # If the file is already within the configured threshold of the target
 335        # level, skip normalization entirely and copy the input through to the
 336        # output unchanged. This avoids needless re-encoding of files that are
 337        # already at the target level.
 338        if self._is_within_threshold():
 339            self._handle_skip()
 340            return
 341
 342        temp_dir = None
 343
 344        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.replaygain:
 345            _logger.debug(
 346                "ReplayGain mode: Second pass will run with temporary file to get stats."
 347            )
 348            temp_dir = mkdtemp()
 349            self.temp_file = os.path.join(temp_dir, f"out.{self.output_ext}")
 350            self.output_file = self.temp_file
 351
 352        # run the second pass as a whole.
 353        with self.ffmpeg_normalize.progress_display.task("Second pass") as update:
 354            for progress in self._second_pass():
 355                update(progress)
 356
 357        # remove temp dir; this will remove the temp file as well if it has not been renamed (e.g. for replaygain)
 358        if temp_dir and os.path.exists(temp_dir):
 359            rmtree(temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)
 360
 361        # This will use stats from ebu_pass2 if available (from the main second pass),
 362        # or fall back to ebu_pass1.
 363        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.replaygain:
 364            _logger.debug(
 365                "ReplayGain tagging is enabled. Proceeding with tag calculation/application."
 366            )
 367            self._run_replaygain()
 368        else:
 369            # Strip any existing ReplayGain tags from the output file
 370            # since they are no longer accurate after normalization
 371            self._strip_replaygain_tags(self.output_file)
 372            # Copy input timestamps last, after any tag modifications, so the
 373            # output ends up with the original modification time.
 374            if self.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_mtime and not self.ffmpeg_normalize.dry_run:
 375                self._apply_input_timestamps()
 376            _logger.info(f"Normalized file written to {self.output_file}")
 377
 378    def verify_output(self) -> None:
 379        """Verify encoded audio, restoring requested timestamps after reading it."""
 380        try:
 381            self._verify_output()
 382        finally:
 383            if self.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_mtime:
 384                self._apply_input_timestamps()
 385
 386    def _verify_output(self) -> None:
 387        """Measure encoded audio without reapplying filters or input options.
 388
 389        Only normalized streams are checked. They precede passthrough and
 390        original audio in encoded outputs; skipped files retain input indices.
 391        Verification keeps the encoded file even if a check fails.
 392        """
 393        config = copy(self.ffmpeg_normalize)
 394        config.pre_filter = config.post_filter = None
 395        config.extra_input_options = None
 396        config.audio_channels = None
 397        measured_file = MediaFile(config, self.output_file, os.devnull)
 398        selected = self._get_streams_to_normalize()
 399        output_streams = list(measured_file.streams["audio"].values())
 400        if self.status == "skipped":
 401            output_streams = [
 402                measured_file.streams["audio"][stream.stream_id] for stream in selected
 403            ]
 404        if not selected or len(output_streams) < len(selected):
 405            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
 406                "Cannot verify output: selected audio streams are missing"
 407            )
 408
 409        failures: list[str] = []
 410        for source, measured in zip(selected, output_streams):
 411            summary = source.get_summary()
 412            expected = summary["output_level"]
 413            if config.normalization_type == "ebu":
 414                for _ in measured.parse_loudnorm_stats():
 415                    pass
 416                stats = measured.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]
 417                if stats is None:
 418                    raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
 419                        "Cannot verify output: loudness measurement is missing"
 420                    )
 421                level, peak = float(stats["input_i"]), float(stats["input_tp"])
 422                if self.status != "skipped":
 423                    expected = source.verification_target_level
 424                    if expected is None:
 425                        expected = summary["input_level"]
 426                peak_limit = config.true_peak
 427            else:
 428                for _ in measured.parse_astats():
 429                    pass
 430                level = measured.loudness_statistics[
 431                    "mean" if config.normalization_type == "rms" else "max"
 432                ]
 433                peak = measured.loudness_statistics["max"]
 434                peak_limit = (
 435                    config.target_level if config.normalization_type == "peak" else 0.0
 436                )
 437
 438            if self.status == "skipped" and summary["output_peak"] is not None:
 439                peak_limit = summary["output_peak"]
 440
 441            def finite(value: float | None) -> float | None:
 442                return value if value is not None and math.isfinite(value) else None
 443
 444            level, peak, expected = finite(level), finite(peak), finite(expected)
 445            errors: list[str] = []
 446            if level is None or expected is None:
 447                errors.append("output level or expected level is not finite")
 448            elif abs(level - expected) > config.verify_loudness_tolerance:
 449                errors.append(
 450                    f"level {level:.2f} differs from expected {expected:.2f} "
 451                    f"by more than {config.verify_loudness_tolerance:g} dB/LU"
 452                )
 453            if peak is None:
 454                errors.append("output peak is not finite")
 455            elif peak > peak_limit + config.verify_peak_tolerance:
 456                errors.append(
 457                    f"peak {peak:.2f} exceeds ceiling {peak_limit:.2f} "
 458                    f"plus {config.verify_peak_tolerance:g} dB tolerance"
 459                )
 460            result: VerificationResult = {
 461                "output_stream_id": measured.stream_id,
 462                "output_level": level,
 463                "output_peak": peak,
 464                "expected_level": expected,
 465                "peak_limit": peak_limit,
 466                "loudness_tolerance": config.verify_loudness_tolerance,
 467                "peak_tolerance": config.verify_peak_tolerance,
 468                "passed": not errors,
 469                "errors": errors,
 470            }
 471            source.verification = result
 472            if errors:
 473                failures.append(f"stream {source.stream_id}: " + "; ".join(errors))
 474        if failures:
 475            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
 476                "Encoded-output verification failed: " + "; ".join(failures)
 477            )
 478        _logger.info(f"Encoded-output verification passed for {self.output_file}")
 479
 480    def _is_within_threshold(self) -> bool:
 481        """
 482        Return whether every stream selected for normalization is already
 483        within the configured threshold of the target level, meaning the file
 484        can be copied through unchanged instead of being re-normalized.
 485
 486        The check compares the measured level against the absolute target level
 487        (integrated loudness for EBU, peak/RMS level otherwise). It is disabled
 488        when the threshold is zero or less, in batch mode (where files are
 489        adjusted relative to a shared reference rather than an absolute target),
 490        in ReplayGain mode (which only writes tags), when a pre/post filter or
 491        channel downmix is requested (since these change the audio), and when
 492        the output extension differs from the input (since the file is copied
 493        verbatim, a container change would otherwise produce an invalid file).
 494
 495        Returns:
 496            bool: True if the file should be skipped, False otherwise.
 497        """
 498        threshold = self.ffmpeg_normalize.threshold
 499        if threshold <= 0:
 500            return False
 501
 502        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.batch or self.ffmpeg_normalize.replaygain:
 503            return False
 504
 505        if (
 506            self.ffmpeg_normalize.pre_filter
 507            or self.ffmpeg_normalize.post_filter
 508            or self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_channels
 509        ):
 510            return False
 511
 512        # A skipped file is copied verbatim, which only yields a valid file when
 513        # the container stays the same. If the output extension differs, fall
 514        # back to normal normalization so the requested format is produced.
 515        input_ext = os.path.splitext(self.input_file)[1][1:].lower()
 516        if input_ext != self.output_ext.lower():
 517            return False
 518
 519        norm_type = self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type
 520        target = self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level
 521        streams = self._get_streams_to_normalize()
 522        if not streams:
 523            return False
 524
 525        for stream in streams:
 526            measured: float | None
 527            if norm_type == "ebu":
 528                ebu_stats = stream.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]
 529                if ebu_stats is None:
 530                    return False
 531                measured = ebu_stats["input_i"]
 532            elif norm_type == "peak":
 533                measured = stream.loudness_statistics["max"]
 534            else:  # rms
 535                measured = stream.loudness_statistics["mean"]
 536
 537            if measured is None:
 538                return False
 539            if abs(target - float(measured)) > threshold:
 540                return False
 541
 542        return True
 543
 544    def _handle_skip(self) -> None:
 545        """
 546        Mark this file as skipped (already at target) and copy the input
 547        through to the output unchanged.
 548
 549        The input is copied verbatim (codec and other output options are not
 550        applied to skipped files; use a threshold of 0 to always re-encode).
 551        Stale ReplayGain tags are still stripped from the output, and the input
 552        modification time is preserved if requested.
 553        """
 554        self.status = "skipped"
 555        _logger.info(
 556            f"{self.input_file}: already within {self.ffmpeg_normalize.threshold} "
 557            f"of target level {self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level}, "
 558            "skipping normalization"
 559        )
 560
 561        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.dry_run:
 562            _logger.warning("Dry run used, not actually copying the file")
 563            return
 564
 565        if self.output_file == os.devnull:
 566            return
 567
 568        if os.path.realpath(self.input_file) != os.path.realpath(self.output_file):
 569            try:
 570                copyfile(self.input_file, self.output_file)
 571            except OSError as e:
 572                raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
 573                    f"Could not copy {self.input_file} to {self.output_file}: {e}"
 574                )
 575        else:
 576            _logger.debug(
 577                "Output file is the same as the input file, leaving it unchanged"
 578            )
 579
 580        # Remove any existing ReplayGain tags from the output, matching the
 581        # behavior of a normal run.
 582        self._strip_replaygain_tags(self.output_file)
 583
 584        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_mtime:
 585            self._apply_input_timestamps()
 586
 587        _logger.info(f"Skipped file copied to {self.output_file}")
 588
 589    def _apply_input_timestamps(self) -> None:
 590        """
 591        Copy the input file's access and modification times to the output file.
 592
 593        Used when the ``keep_mtime`` option is enabled. Only the access and
 594        modification times are copied; a file's creation time (which some
 595        operating systems such as Windows track separately) is not affected.
 596        """
 597        if self.input_timestamps is None:
 598            return
 599        atime, mtime = self.input_timestamps
 600        try:
 601            os.utime(self.output_file, (atime, mtime))
 602            _logger.debug(
 603                f"Copied input timestamps to {self.output_file} "
 604                f"(atime={atime}, mtime={mtime})"
 605            )
 606        except OSError as e:
 607            _logger.warning(f"Could not copy timestamps to {self.output_file}: {e}")
 608
 609    def _run_replaygain(self) -> None:
 610        """
 611        Run the replaygain process for this file.
 612        """
 613        _logger.debug(f"Running replaygain for {self.input_file}")
 614
 615        # get the audio streams
 616        audio_streams = list(self.streams["audio"].values())
 617
 618        # Attempt to use EBU pass 2 statistics, which account for pre-filters.
 619        # These are populated by the main second pass if it runs (not a dry run)
 620        # and normalization_type is 'ebu'.
 621        loudness_stats_source = "ebu_pass2"
 622        loudnorm_stats = audio_streams[0].loudness_statistics.get("ebu_pass2")
 623
 624        if loudnorm_stats is None:
 625            _logger.warning(
 626                "ReplayGain: Second pass EBU statistics (ebu_pass2) not found. "
 627                "Falling back to first pass EBU statistics (ebu_pass1). "
 628                "This may not account for pre-filters if any are used."
 629            )
 630            loudness_stats_source = "ebu_pass1"
 631            loudnorm_stats = audio_streams[0].loudness_statistics.get("ebu_pass1")
 632
 633        if loudnorm_stats is None:
 634            _logger.error(
 635                f"ReplayGain: No loudness statistics available from {loudness_stats_source} (and fallback) for stream 0. "
 636                "Cannot calculate ReplayGain tags."
 637            )
 638            return
 639
 640        _logger.debug(
 641            f"Using statistics from {loudness_stats_source} for ReplayGain calculation."
 642        )
 643
 644        # apply the replaygain tag from the first audio stream (to all audio streams)
 645        if len(audio_streams) > 1:
 646            _logger.warning(
 647                f"Your input file has {len(audio_streams)} audio streams. "
 648                "Only the first audio stream's replaygain tag will be applied. "
 649                "All audio streams will receive the same tag."
 650            )
 651
 652        target_level = self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level
 653        # Use 'input_i' and 'input_tp' from the chosen stats.
 654        # For ebu_pass2, these are measurements *after* pre-filter but *before* loudnorm adjustment.
 655        input_i = loudnorm_stats.get("input_i")
 656        input_tp = loudnorm_stats.get("input_tp")
 657
 658        if input_i is None or input_tp is None:
 659            _logger.error(
 660                f"ReplayGain: 'input_i' or 'input_tp' missing from {loudness_stats_source} statistics. "
 661                "Cannot calculate ReplayGain tags."
 662            )
 663            return
 664
 665        track_gain = -(input_i - target_level)  # dB
 666        track_peak = 10 ** (input_tp / 20)  # linear scale
 667
 668        _logger.debug(f"Calculated Track gain: {track_gain:.2f} dB")
 669        _logger.debug(f"Calculated Track peak: {track_peak:.2f}")
 670
 671        if not self.ffmpeg_normalize.dry_run:  # This uses the overall dry_run state
 672            self._write_replaygain_tags(track_gain, track_peak)
 673        else:
 674            _logger.warning(
 675                "Overall dry_run is enabled, not actually writing ReplayGain tags to the file. "
 676                "Tag calculation based on available stats was performed."
 677            )
 678
 679    def _write_replaygain_tags(self, track_gain: float, track_peak: float) -> None:
 680        """
 681        Write the replaygain tags to the input file.
 682
 683        This is based on the code from bohning/usdb_syncer, licensed under the MIT license.
 684        See: https://github.com/bohning/usdb_syncer/blob/2fa638c4f487dffe9f5364f91e156ba54cb20233/src/usdb_syncer/resource_dl.py
 685        """
 686        _logger.debug(f"Writing ReplayGain tags to {self.input_file}")
 687
 688        input_file_ext = os.path.splitext(self.input_file)[1]
 689        if input_file_ext == ".mp3":
 690            mp3 = MP3(self.input_file, ID3=ID3)
 691            if not mp3.tags:
 692                return
 693            mp3.tags.add(
 694                TXXX(desc="REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_GAIN", text=[f"{track_gain:.2f} dB"])
 695            )
 696            mp3.tags.add(TXXX(desc="REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_PEAK", text=[f"{track_peak:.6f}"]))
 697            mp3.save()
 698        elif input_file_ext in [".mp4", ".m4a", ".m4v", ".mov"]:
 699            mp4 = MP4(self.input_file)
 700            if not mp4.tags:
 701                mp4.add_tags()
 702            if not mp4.tags:
 703                return
 704            mp4.tags["----:com.apple.iTunes:REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_GAIN"] = [
 705                f"{track_gain:.2f} dB".encode()
 706            ]
 707            mp4.tags["----:com.apple.iTunes:REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_PEAK"] = [
 708                f"{track_peak:.6f}".encode()
 709            ]
 710            mp4.save()
 711        elif input_file_ext == ".ogg":
 712            ogg = OggVorbis(self.input_file)
 713            ogg["REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_GAIN"] = [f"{track_gain:.2f} dB"]
 714            ogg["REPLAYGAIN_TRACK_PEAK"] = [f"{track_peak:.6f}"]
 715            ogg.save()
 716        elif input_file_ext == ".opus":
 717            opus = OggOpus(self.input_file)
 718            # See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7845#section-5.2.1
 719            opus["R128_TRACK_GAIN"] = [str(round(256 * track_gain))]
 720            opus.save()
 721        else:
 722            _logger.error(
 723                f"Unsupported input file extension: {input_file_ext} for writing replaygain tags. "
 724                "Only .mp3, .mp4/.m4a, .ogg, .opus are supported. "
 725                "If you think this should support more formats, please let me know at "
 726                "https://github.com/slhck/ffmpeg-normalize/issues"
 727            )
 728            return
 729
 730        _logger.info(
 731            f"Successfully wrote replaygain tags to input file {self.input_file}"
 732        )
 733
 734    def _strip_replaygain_tags(self, output_file: str) -> None:
 735        """
 736        Strip ReplayGain tags from the output file after normalization.
 737
 738        This ensures that old ReplayGain tags from the input are removed,
 739        since they are no longer accurate after normalization.
 740
 741        Args:
 742            output_file (str): Path to the output file to strip tags from
 743        """
 744        _logger.debug(f"Stripping ReplayGain tags from {output_file}")
 745
 746        output_file_ext = os.path.splitext(output_file)[1]
 747        if output_file_ext == ".mp3":
 748            try:
 749                mp3 = MP3(output_file, ID3=ID3)
 750                if not mp3.tags:
 751                    return
 752                # Remove REPLAYGAIN_* tags
 753                tags_to_remove = [
 754                    key for key in mp3.tags if key.startswith("TXXX:REPLAYGAIN_")
 755                ]
 756                for tag in tags_to_remove:
 757                    del mp3.tags[tag]
 758                if tags_to_remove:
 759                    mp3.save()
 760                    _logger.debug(
 761                        f"Stripped {len(tags_to_remove)} ReplayGain tag(s) from {output_file}"
 762                    )
 763            except Exception as e:
 764                _logger.warning(
 765                    f"Could not strip ReplayGain tags from {output_file}: {e}"
 766                )
 767        elif output_file_ext in [".mp4", ".m4a", ".m4v", ".mov"]:
 768            try:
 769                mp4 = MP4(output_file)
 770                if not mp4.tags:
 771                    return
 772                # Remove REPLAYGAIN_* tags
 773                tags_to_remove = [
 774                    key
 775                    for key in mp4.tags
 776                    if "REPLAYGAIN_" in key.upper() or "REPLAYGAIN" in key.upper()
 777                ]
 778                for tag in tags_to_remove:
 779                    del mp4.tags[tag]
 780                if tags_to_remove:
 781                    mp4.save()
 782                    _logger.debug(
 783                        f"Stripped {len(tags_to_remove)} ReplayGain tag(s) from {output_file}"
 784                    )
 785            except Exception as e:
 786                _logger.warning(
 787                    f"Could not strip ReplayGain tags from {output_file}: {e}"
 788                )
 789        elif output_file_ext == ".ogg":
 790            try:
 791                ogg = OggVorbis(output_file)
 792                # Remove REPLAYGAIN_* tags (case-insensitive)
 793                tags_to_remove = [
 794                    key for key in ogg.keys() if key.upper().startswith("REPLAYGAIN_")
 795                ]
 796                for tag in tags_to_remove:
 797                    del ogg[tag]
 798                if tags_to_remove:
 799                    ogg.save()
 800                    _logger.debug(
 801                        f"Stripped {len(tags_to_remove)} ReplayGain tag(s) from {output_file}"
 802                    )
 803            except Exception as e:
 804                _logger.warning(
 805                    f"Could not strip ReplayGain tags from {output_file}: {e}"
 806                )
 807        elif output_file_ext == ".opus":
 808            try:
 809                opus = OggOpus(output_file)
 810                # Remove R128_* tags (Opus uses R128 instead of REPLAYGAIN, case-insensitive)
 811                tags_to_remove = [
 812                    key for key in opus.keys() if key.upper().startswith("R128_")
 813                ]
 814                for tag in tags_to_remove:
 815                    del opus[tag]
 816                if tags_to_remove:
 817                    opus.save()
 818                    _logger.debug(
 819                        f"Stripped {len(tags_to_remove)} R128 tag(s) from {output_file}"
 820                    )
 821            except Exception as e:
 822                _logger.warning(
 823                    f"Could not strip ReplayGain tags from {output_file}: {e}"
 824                )
 825        else:
 826            # For other formats, we don't need to strip tags
 827            _logger.debug(
 828                f"Skipping ReplayGain tag stripping for {output_file_ext} (not supported/needed)"
 829            )
 830
 831    def _can_write_output_video(self) -> bool:
 832        """
 833        Determine whether the output file can contain video at all.
 834
 835        Returns:
 836            bool: True if the output file can contain video, False otherwise
 837        """
 838        if self.output_ext.lower() in AUDIO_ONLY_FORMATS:
 839            return False
 840
 841        return not self.ffmpeg_normalize.video_disable
 842
 843    def _first_pass(self) -> None:
 844        """
 845        Run the first pass of the normalization process.
 846        """
 847        _logger.debug(f"Parsing normalization info for {self.input_file}")
 848
 849        streams_to_normalize = self._get_streams_to_normalize()
 850
 851        for index, audio_stream in enumerate(streams_to_normalize):
 852            if self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type == "ebu":
 853                fun = getattr(audio_stream, "parse_loudnorm_stats")
 854            else:
 855                fun = getattr(audio_stream, "parse_astats")
 856
 857            description = f"First pass, stream {index + 1}/{len(streams_to_normalize)}"
 858            with self.ffmpeg_normalize.progress_display.task(description) as update:
 859                for progress in fun():
 860                    update(progress)
 861
 862    def _get_stream_filter_chain(self, audio_stream: AudioStream) -> list[str]:
 863        """
 864        Return the ordered list of ffmpeg audio filters applied to a single
 865        stream in the second pass: the optional pre-filter, channel conversion,
 866        the normalization filter itself (loudnorm for EBU, or the volume /
 867        dynaudnorm filter for peak / RMS), and the optional post-filter.
 868
 869        Returns:
 870            list[str]: the filters, in application order
 871        """
 872        skip_normalization = False
 873        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.lower_only and not (
 874            self.batch_reference is not None
 875            and self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type in ("peak", "rms")
 876        ):
 877            if self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type == "ebu":
 878                if (
 879                    audio_stream.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"] is not None
 880                    and audio_stream.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_i"]
 881                    < self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level
 882                ):
 883                    skip_normalization = True
 884            elif self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type == "peak":
 885                if (
 886                    audio_stream.loudness_statistics["max"] is not None
 887                    and audio_stream.loudness_statistics["max"]
 888                    < self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level
 889                ):
 890                    skip_normalization = True
 891            elif self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type == "rms":
 892                if (
 893                    audio_stream.loudness_statistics["mean"] is not None
 894                    and audio_stream.loudness_statistics["mean"]
 895                    < self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level
 896                ):
 897                    skip_normalization = True
 898
 899        if skip_normalization:
 900            _logger.warning(
 901                f"Stream {audio_stream.stream_id} had measured input loudness lower than target, skipping normalization."
 902            )
 903            normalization_filter = "acopy"
 904            audio_stream.applied_gain = 0.0
 905        else:
 906            if self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type == "ebu":
 907                normalization_filter = audio_stream.get_second_pass_opts_ebu(
 908                    batch_reference=self.batch_reference
 909                )
 910            else:
 911                normalization_filter = audio_stream.get_second_pass_opts_peakrms(
 912                    batch_reference=self.batch_reference
 913                )
 914
 915        filter_chain = []
 916
 917        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.pre_filter:
 918            filter_chain.append(self.ffmpeg_normalize.pre_filter)
 919
 920        # Apply channel conversion before normalization so that the
 921        # normalization filter operates on the same channel layout that
 922        # was measured in the first pass. See issue #316.
 923        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_channels:
 924            filter_chain.append(
 925                f"aformat=sample_fmts=fltp:channel_layouts={self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_channels}c"
 926            )
 927
 928        filter_chain.append(normalization_filter)
 929
 930        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.post_filter:
 931            filter_chain.append(self.ffmpeg_normalize.post_filter)
 932
 933        return filter_chain
 934
 935    def _get_audio_filter_cmd(self) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
 936        """
 937        Return the audio filter command and output labels needed.
 938
 939        Returns:
 940            tuple[str, list[str]]: filter_complex command and the required output labels
 941        """
 942        filter_chains = []
 943        output_labels = []
 944
 945        self._stream_filter_chains = {}
 946
 947        for audio_stream in self._get_streams_to_normalize():
 948            filter_chain = self._get_stream_filter_chain(audio_stream)
 949            self._stream_filter_chains[audio_stream.stream_id] = filter_chain
 950
 951            input_label = f"[0:{audio_stream.stream_id}]"
 952            output_label = f"[norm{audio_stream.stream_id}]"
 953            output_labels.append(output_label)
 954
 955            filter_chains.append(input_label + ",".join(filter_chain) + output_label)
 956
 957        filter_complex_cmd = ";".join(filter_chains)
 958
 959        return filter_complex_cmd, output_labels
 960
 961    def _get_encoder_settings(
 962        self, audio_stream: AudioStream, audio_codec: str | None
 963    ) -> str:
 964        """
 965        Return an ffmpeg-command-equivalent description of how a single audio
 966        stream is encoded in the second pass: the codec, then the bitrate,
 967        sample rate and channel count when set, followed by the effective
 968        filter chain (which includes the loudnorm measured values).
 969
 970        Written as the ``ENCODER_SETTINGS`` stream tag when
 971        ``write_encoder_settings`` is enabled. The filter chain comes from the
 972        cache populated by :meth:`_get_audio_filter_cmd`, which must run first.
 973        The loudnorm ``print_format`` option is dropped, as it only controls
 974        first-pass diagnostics and not the normalization itself.
 975
 976        Returns:
 977            str: e.g. ``-c:a libopus -b:a 128000 -af loudnorm=i=-23.0:...``
 978        """
 979        codec = audio_codec if audio_codec else audio_stream.get_pcm_codec()
 980        args = ["-c:a", codec]
 981        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_bitrate:
 982            args += ["-b:a", str(self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_bitrate)]
 983        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.sample_rate:
 984            args += ["-ar", str(self.ffmpeg_normalize.sample_rate)]
 985        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_channels:
 986            args += ["-ac", str(self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_channels)]
 987        filter_chain = self._stream_filter_chains.get(audio_stream.stream_id, [])
 988        if filter_chain:
 989            af = re.sub(r":print_format=\w+", "", ",".join(filter_chain))
 990            args += ["-af", af]
 991        return shlex.join(args)
 992
 993    def _get_audio_codec(self) -> str | None:
 994        """
 995        Return the audio encoder to use for normalized streams, or None to use
 996        the bit-depth-aware PCM default.
 997
 998        An explicit ``--audio-codec`` (``-c:a``) always takes precedence.
 999        Otherwise, for a container that cannot store PCM (e.g. FLAC, MP3, Opus),
1000        fall back to the codec ffmpeg itself would default to for that container,
1001        so audio-only outputs work without requiring ``-c:a``. PCM-friendly
1002        containers (e.g. WAV, Matroska) keep the lossless PCM default regardless
1003        of their own muxer default.
1004
1005        Returns:
1006            str | None: The encoder name, or None to use the PCM default.
1007        """
1008        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_codec:
1009            return self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_codec
1010
1011        output_format = self.ffmpeg_normalize.output_format
1012        if output_format in PCM_INCOMPATIBLE_FORMATS:
1013            container = output_format
1014        elif self.output_ext.lower() in PCM_INCOMPATIBLE_EXTS:
1015            container = self.output_ext
1016        else:
1017            return None
1018
1019        encoder = get_muxer_default_audio_encoder(container)
1020        if encoder is not None:
1021            _logger.debug(
1022                f"No audio codec set; using ffmpeg's default '{encoder}' for "
1023                f"container '{container}'"
1024            )
1025        return encoder
1026
1027    def _second_pass(self) -> Iterator[float]:
1028        """
1029        Construct the second pass command and run it.
1030
1031        FIXME: make this method simpler
1032        """
1033        _logger.info(f"Running second pass for {self.input_file}")
1034
1035        # get the target output stream types depending on the options
1036        output_stream_types: list[Literal["audio", "video", "subtitle"]] = ["audio"]
1037        if self._can_write_output_video():
1038            output_stream_types.append("video")
1039        if not self.ffmpeg_normalize.subtitle_disable:
1040            output_stream_types.append("subtitle")
1041
1042        # base command, here we will add all other options
1043        cmd = [self.ffmpeg_normalize.ffmpeg_exe, "-hide_banner", "-y"]
1044
1045        # extra options (if any)
1046        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_input_options:
1047            cmd.extend(self.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_input_options)
1048
1049        # get complex filter command
1050        audio_filter_cmd, output_labels = self._get_audio_filter_cmd()
1051
1052        # add input file and basic filter
1053        cmd.extend(["-i", self.input_file, "-filter_complex", audio_filter_cmd])
1054
1055        # map metadata, only if needed
1056        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.metadata_disable:
1057            cmd.extend(["-map_metadata", "-1"])
1058        else:
1059            # map global metadata
1060            cmd.extend(["-map_metadata", "0"])
1061            # map per-stream metadata (e.g. language tags)
1062            for stream_type in output_stream_types:
1063                stream_key = stream_type[0]
1064                if stream_type not in self.streams:
1065                    continue
1066                for idx, _ in enumerate(self.streams[stream_type].items()):
1067                    cmd.extend(
1068                        [
1069                            f"-map_metadata:s:{stream_key}:{idx}",
1070                            f"0:s:{stream_key}:{idx}",
1071                        ]
1072                    )
1073
1074        # map chapters if needed
1075        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.chapters_disable:
1076            cmd.extend(["-map_chapters", "-1"])
1077        else:
1078            cmd.extend(["-map_chapters", "0"])
1079
1080        # collect all '-map' and codecs needed for output video based on input video
1081        if self.streams["video"]:
1082            if self._can_write_output_video():
1083                for s in self.streams["video"].keys():
1084                    cmd.extend(["-map", f"0:{s}"])
1085                # set codec (copy by default)
1086                cmd.extend(["-c:v", self.ffmpeg_normalize.video_codec])
1087            else:
1088                if not self.ffmpeg_normalize.video_disable:
1089                    _logger.warning(
1090                        f"The chosen output extension {self.output_ext} does not support video/cover art. It will be disabled."
1091                    )
1092
1093        # Determine streams to normalize and passthrough
1094        streams_to_normalize = self._get_streams_to_normalize()
1095        all_audio_streams = list(self.streams["audio"].values())
1096
1097        # Determine which streams to passthrough
1098        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_other_audio and (
1099            self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_streams is not None
1100            or self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_default_only
1101        ):
1102            streams_to_passthrough = [
1103                s for s in all_audio_streams if s not in streams_to_normalize
1104            ]
1105        else:
1106            streams_to_passthrough = []
1107
1108        # ... and map the output of the normalization filters
1109        for ol in output_labels:
1110            cmd.extend(["-map", ol])
1111
1112        # ... and map passthrough audio streams (copy without normalization)
1113        for stream in streams_to_passthrough:
1114            cmd.extend(["-map", f"0:{stream.stream_id}"])
1115
1116        # Track output audio stream index for codec assignment
1117        output_audio_idx = 0
1118
1119        # Resolve the audio codec once: an explicit --audio-codec wins, otherwise
1120        # fall back to ffmpeg's own default codec for the output container (None
1121        # means use the bit-depth-aware PCM default).
1122        audio_codec = self._get_audio_codec()
1123
1124        # set audio codec for normalized streams
1125        for audio_stream in streams_to_normalize:
1126            codec = audio_codec if audio_codec else audio_stream.get_pcm_codec()
1127            cmd.extend([f"-c:a:{output_audio_idx}", codec])
1128            output_audio_idx += 1
1129
1130        # set audio codec for passthrough streams (always copy)
1131        for _ in streams_to_passthrough:
1132            cmd.extend([f"-c:a:{output_audio_idx}", "copy"])
1133            output_audio_idx += 1
1134
1135        # other audio options (if any) - only apply to normalized streams
1136        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_bitrate:
1137            if audio_codec == "libvorbis":
1138                # libvorbis takes just a "-b" option, for some reason
1139                # https://github.com/slhck/ffmpeg-normalize/issues/277
1140                cmd.extend(["-b", str(self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_bitrate)])
1141            else:
1142                # Only apply to normalized streams
1143                for idx in range(len(streams_to_normalize)):
1144                    cmd.extend(
1145                        [f"-b:a:{idx}", str(self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_bitrate)]
1146                    )
1147        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.sample_rate:
1148            # Only apply to normalized streams
1149            for idx in range(len(streams_to_normalize)):
1150                cmd.extend([f"-ar:a:{idx}", str(self.ffmpeg_normalize.sample_rate)])
1151        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_channels:
1152            # Only apply to normalized streams
1153            for idx in range(len(streams_to_normalize)):
1154                cmd.extend([f"-ac:a:{idx}", str(self.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_channels)])
1155
1156        # record how each normalized stream was encoded as an ENCODER_SETTINGS
1157        # tag (a Matroska/WebM convention), so the output documents itself
1158        if (
1159            self.ffmpeg_normalize.write_encoder_settings
1160            and not self.ffmpeg_normalize.metadata_disable
1161        ):
1162            for idx, audio_stream in enumerate(streams_to_normalize):
1163                cmd.extend(
1164                    [
1165                        f"-metadata:s:a:{idx}",
1166                        "ENCODER_SETTINGS="
1167                        + self._get_encoder_settings(audio_stream, audio_codec),
1168                    ]
1169                )
1170
1171        # carry the input bit depth through to the output encoder, if requested
1172        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_bit_depth:
1173            for idx, audio_stream in enumerate(streams_to_normalize):
1174                sample_fmt = audio_stream.get_output_sample_fmt(audio_codec)
1175                if sample_fmt is not None:
1176                    cmd.extend([f"-sample_fmt:a:{idx}", sample_fmt])
1177
1178        # ... and subtitles
1179        if not self.ffmpeg_normalize.subtitle_disable:
1180            for s in self.streams["subtitle"].keys():
1181                cmd.extend(["-map", f"0:{s}"])
1182            # copy subtitles
1183            cmd.extend(["-c:s", "copy"])
1184
1185        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_original_audio:
1186            # Map all original audio streams after normalized and passthrough streams
1187            for index, _ in enumerate(self.streams["audio"].items()):
1188                cmd.extend(["-map", f"0:a:{index}"])
1189                cmd.extend([f"-c:a:{output_audio_idx}", "copy"])
1190                output_audio_idx += 1
1191
1192        # extra options (if any)
1193        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_output_options:
1194            cmd.extend(self.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_output_options)
1195
1196        # output format (if any)
1197        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.output_format:
1198            cmd.extend(["-f", self.ffmpeg_normalize.output_format])
1199
1200        # if dry run, only show sample command
1201        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.dry_run:
1202            cmd.append(self.output_file)
1203            _logger.warning("Dry run used, not actually running second-pass command")
1204            CommandRunner(dry=True).run_command(cmd)
1205            yield 100
1206            return
1207
1208        is_in_place_overwrite = os.path.realpath(self.input_file) == os.path.realpath(
1209            self.output_file
1210        )
1211
1212        temp_file: Union[str, None] = None
1213        if is_in_place_overwrite:
1214            # need to create a temporary file because we cannot override
1215            # the same input file
1216            output_dir = os.path.dirname(self.output_file) or "."
1217            fd, temp_file = mkstemp(
1218                suffix=f".{self.output_ext}",
1219                prefix=f".{os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(self.output_file))[0]}.",
1220                dir=output_dir,
1221            )
1222            os.close(fd)
1223            # mkstemp creates the file with mode 0600; keep the input's mode
1224            copymode(self.input_file, temp_file)
1225            _logger.debug(
1226                f"Output file is the same as the input file, "
1227                f"encoding to temporary file {temp_file} first"
1228            )
1229            cmd.append(temp_file)
1230        else:
1231            cmd.append(self.output_file)
1232
1233        cmd_runner = CommandRunner()
1234        try:
1235            yield from cmd_runner.run_ffmpeg_command(cmd)
1236        except Exception as e:
1237            if temp_file and os.path.exists(temp_file):
1238                os.remove(temp_file)
1239            raise e
1240        else:
1241            # for in-place normalization, move the finished temp file over the input
1242            if temp_file:
1243                _logger.debug(
1244                    f"Moving temporary file from {temp_file} to {self.output_file}"
1245                )
1246                os.replace(temp_file, self.output_file)
1247
1248        output = cmd_runner.get_output()
1249        # in the second pass, we do not normalize stream-by-stream, so we set the stats based on the
1250        # overall output (which includes multiple loudnorm stats)
1251        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type == "ebu":
1252            ebu_pass_2_stats = list(
1253                AudioStream.prune_and_parse_loudnorm_output(output).values()
1254            )
1255            # Only set second pass stats for streams that were actually normalized
1256            streams_to_normalize = self._get_streams_to_normalize()
1257            if len(ebu_pass_2_stats) == len(streams_to_normalize):
1258                for idx, audio_stream in enumerate(streams_to_normalize):
1259                    audio_stream.set_second_pass_stats(ebu_pass_2_stats[idx])
1260            else:
1261                _logger.debug(
1262                    f"Expected {len(streams_to_normalize)} EBU pass 2 statistics but got {len(ebu_pass_2_stats)}. "
1263                    "This can happen when normalization is skipped (e.g., with --lower-only)."
1264                )
1265
1266        # warn if dynamic == False and any of the second pass stats contain "normalization_type" == "dynamic"
1267        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.dynamic is False:
1268            for audio_stream in self.streams["audio"].values():
1269                pass2_stats = audio_stream.get_stats()["ebu_pass2"]
1270                if pass2_stats is None:
1271                    continue
1272                if pass2_stats["normalization_type"] == "dynamic":
1273                    pass1_stats = audio_stream.get_stats()["ebu_pass1"]
1274
1275                    reason = ""
1276                    if pass1_stats is not None:
1277                        target_level = audio_stream.verification_target_level
1278                        if target_level is None:
1279                            target_level = self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level
1280                        linear_gain = target_level - pass1_stats["input_i"]
1281                        estimated_tp = pass1_stats["input_tp"] + linear_gain
1282                        if estimated_tp > self.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak:
1283                            min_tp = estimated_tp
1284                            max_target = (
1285                                self.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak
1286                                - pass1_stats["input_tp"]
1287                                + pass1_stats["input_i"]
1288                            )
1289                            reason = (
1290                                f" Reason: the input true peak ({pass1_stats['input_tp']:.2f} dBTP) is too high — "
1291                                f"after linear gain of {linear_gain:.2f} dB, "
1292                                f"the estimated true peak would be {estimated_tp:.2f} dBTP, "
1293                                f"exceeding the target of {self.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak} dBTP. "
1294                                f"To avoid this, raise --true-peak (-tp) to at least {min_tp:.1f}, "
1295                                f"or lower the target level (-t) to at most {max_target:.1f}."
1296                            )
1297                        elif (
1298                            pass1_stats["input_lra"]
1299                            > self.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target
1300                        ):
1301                            reason = (
1302                                f" Reason: the input loudness range ({pass1_stats['input_lra']:.2f} LU) "
1303                                f"exceeds the target ({self.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target:.2f} LU). "
1304                                "Consider raising the target loudness range or using "
1305                                "--keep-loudness-range-target / --keep-lra-above-loudness-range-target."
1306                            )
1307                        elif pass1_stats["input_lra"] == 0:
1308                            reason = (
1309                                " Reason: the measured input loudness range is zero; "
1310                                "the loudnorm filter requires a nonzero measured range for linear normalization."
1311                            )
1312
1313                    _logger.warning(
1314                        f"{self.input_file}: You specified linear normalization, but the loudnorm filter "
1315                        f"reverted to dynamic normalization.{reason}"
1316                    )
1317
1318        _logger.debug("Normalization finished")
1319
1320    def get_stats(self) -> Iterable[LoudnessStatisticsWithMetadata]:
1321        return (
1322            audio_stream.get_stats() for audio_stream in self.streams["audio"].values()
1323        )
1324
1325    def get_summary(self) -> list[SummaryRow]:
1326        """
1327        Return the before/after summary for each analyzed audio stream.
1328
1329        Streams without any measurement (e.g. streams not selected for
1330        normalization) are left out, unless the file failed to process.
1331
1332        Returns:
1333            list[SummaryRow]: One summary entry per audio stream
1334        """
1335        rows = [
1336            audio_stream.get_summary()
1337            for audio_stream in self.streams["audio"].values()
1338        ]
1339        return [
1340            row
1341            for row in rows
1342            if row["status"] == "error" or row["input_level"] is not None
1343        ]

 68    def __init__(
 69        self, ffmpeg_normalize: FFmpegNormalize, input_file: str, output_file: str
 70    ):
 71        """
 72        Initialize a media file for later normalization by parsing the streams.
 73
 74        Args:
 75            ffmpeg_normalize (FFmpegNormalize): reference to overall settings
 76            input_file (str): Path to input file
 77            output_file (str): Path to output file
 78        """
 79        self.ffmpeg_normalize = ffmpeg_normalize
 80        self.skip = False
 81        # Per-file outcome, reported in the --print-stats output: "normalized"
 82        # (default), "skipped" (already within threshold of target), or "error".
 83        # "error" is set by FFmpegNormalize.run_normalization when processing
 84        # fails; on failure, self.error holds the error message.
 85        self.status: str = "normalized"
 86        self.error: str | None = None
 87        self.input_file = input_file
 88        self.output_file = output_file
 89        current_ext = os.path.splitext(output_file)[1][1:]
 90        # we need to check if it's empty, e.g. /dev/null or NUL
 91        if current_ext == "" or self.output_file == os.devnull:
 92            _logger.debug(
 93                f"Current extension is unset, or output file is a null device, using extension: {self.ffmpeg_normalize.extension}"
 94            )
 95            self.output_ext = self.ffmpeg_normalize.extension
 96        else:
 97            _logger.debug(
 98                f"Current extension is set from output file, using extension: {current_ext}"
 99            )
100            self.output_ext = current_ext
101        self.streams: StreamDict = {"audio": {}, "video": {}, "subtitle": {}}
102        self.temp_file: Union[str, None] = None
103        self.batch_reference: float | None = None
104        # Second-pass filter chain per normalized audio stream, keyed by stream
105        # id. Populated by _get_audio_filter_cmd() and reused by
106        # _get_encoder_settings() so the normalization filter is not built twice.
107        self._stream_filter_chains: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
108        # Input (access, modification) times captured before processing, used
109        # when the keep_mtime option is enabled.
110        self.input_timestamps: tuple[float, float] | None = None
111
112        self.parse_streams()

130    def parse_streams(self) -> None:
131        """
132        Try to parse all input streams from file and set them in self.streams.
133
134        Raises:
135            FFmpegNormalizeError: If no audio streams are found
136        """
137        _logger.debug(f"Parsing streams of {self.input_file}")
138
139        cmd = [
140            self.ffmpeg_normalize.ffmpeg_exe,
141            "-i",
142            self.input_file,
143            "-c",
144            "copy",
145            "-t",
146            "0",
147            "-map",
148            "0",
149            "-f",
150            "null",
151            os.devnull,
152        ]
153
154        output = CommandRunner().run_command(cmd).get_output()
155
156        _logger.debug("Stream parsing command output:")
157        _logger.debug(output)
158
159        output_lines = [line.strip() for line in output.split("\n")]
160
161        # First pass: parse disposition flags for each stream
162        stream_dispositions: dict[int, bool] = {}
163
164        for line in output_lines:
165            if line.startswith("Stream"):
166                if stream_id_match := re.search(r"#0:([\d]+)", line):
167                    stream_id = int(stream_id_match.group(1))
168                    # Check if (default) appears on the Stream line
169                    is_default = "(default)" in line
170                    stream_dispositions[stream_id] = is_default
171
172        # Second pass: parse stream information
173        duration = None
174        for line in output_lines:
175            if "Duration" in line:
176                if duration_search := DUR_REGEX.search(line):
177                    duration = _to_ms(**duration_search.groupdict()) / 1000
178                    _logger.debug(f"Found duration: {duration} s")
179                else:
180                    _logger.warning("Could not extract duration from input file!")
181
182            if not line.startswith("Stream"):
183                continue
184
185            if stream_id_match := re.search(r"#0:([\d]+)", line):
186                stream_id = int(stream_id_match.group(1))
187                if stream_id in self._stream_ids():
188                    continue
189            else:
190                continue
191
192            is_default = stream_dispositions.get(stream_id, False)
193
194            if "Audio" in line:
195                _logger.debug(
196                    f"Found audio stream at index {stream_id} (default: {is_default})"
197                )
198                sample_rate_match = re.search(r"(\d+) Hz", line)
199                sample_rate = (
200                    int(sample_rate_match.group(1)) if sample_rate_match else None
201                )
202                bit_depth_match = re.search(r"([sfu])(\d+)(p|le|be)?", line)
203                bit_depth = int(bit_depth_match.group(2)) if bit_depth_match else None
204                is_float = bit_depth_match.group(1) == "f" if bit_depth_match else False
205                self.streams["audio"][stream_id] = AudioStream(
206                    self.ffmpeg_normalize,
207                    self,
208                    stream_id,
209                    sample_rate,
210                    bit_depth,
211                    duration,
212                    is_default,
213                    is_float,
214                )
215
216            elif "Video" in line:
217                _logger.debug(f"Found video stream at index {stream_id}")
218                self.streams["video"][stream_id] = VideoStream(
219                    self.ffmpeg_normalize, self, stream_id
220                )
221
222            elif "Subtitle" in line:
223                _logger.debug(f"Found subtitle stream at index {stream_id}")
224                self.streams["subtitle"][stream_id] = SubtitleStream(
225                    self.ffmpeg_normalize, self, stream_id
226                )
227
228        if not self.streams["audio"]:
229            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
230                f"Input file {self.input_file} does not contain any audio streams"
231            )
232
233        if (
234            self.output_ext.lower() in ONE_STREAM
235            and len(self.streams["audio"].values()) > 1
236        ):
237            _logger.warning(
238                "Output file only supports one stream. Keeping only first audio stream."
239            )
240            first_stream = list(self.streams["audio"].values())[0]
241            self.streams["audio"] = {first_stream.stream_id: first_stream}
242            self.streams["video"] = {}
243            self.streams["subtitle"] = {}

def run_normalization(self, batch_reference: float | None = None) -> None: 
292    def run_normalization(self, batch_reference: float | None = None) -> None:
293        """
294        Run the normalization process for this file.
295
296        Args:
297            batch_reference (float | None, optional): Reference loudness for batch mode.
298                If provided, the first pass is skipped (assumed already done) and this
299                reference is used to calculate relative adjustments. Defaults to None.
300        """
301        _logger.debug(f"Running normalization for {self.input_file}")
302
303        # Store batch reference for use in second pass
304        self.batch_reference = batch_reference
305
306        # Capture the input file's timestamps before processing, since an
307        # in-place overwrite would otherwise lose the original modification time.
308        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_mtime:
309            try:
310                stat = os.stat(self.input_file)
311                self.input_timestamps = (stat.st_atime, stat.st_mtime)
312            except OSError as e:
313                _logger.warning(
314                    f"Could not read timestamps from {self.input_file}: {e}"
315                )
316
317        # run the first pass to get loudness stats, unless in dynamic EBU mode or batch mode
318        # (in batch mode, first pass is already done in FFmpegNormalize.run_normalization)
319        if batch_reference is None:
320            if not (
321                self.ffmpeg_normalize.dynamic
322                and self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type == "ebu"
323            ):
324                self._first_pass()
325            else:
326                _logger.debug(
327                    "Dynamic EBU mode: First pass will not run, as it is not needed."
328                )
329        else:
330            _logger.debug(
331                f"Batch mode: Skipping first pass (already completed), using batch reference = {batch_reference:.2f}"
332            )
333
334        # If the file is already within the configured threshold of the target
335        # level, skip normalization entirely and copy the input through to the
336        # output unchanged. This avoids needless re-encoding of files that are
337        # already at the target level.
338        if self._is_within_threshold():
339            self._handle_skip()
340            return
341
342        temp_dir = None
343
344        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.replaygain:
345            _logger.debug(
346                "ReplayGain mode: Second pass will run with temporary file to get stats."
347            )
348            temp_dir = mkdtemp()
349            self.temp_file = os.path.join(temp_dir, f"out.{self.output_ext}")
350            self.output_file = self.temp_file
351
352        # run the second pass as a whole.
353        with self.ffmpeg_normalize.progress_display.task("Second pass") as update:
354            for progress in self._second_pass():
355                update(progress)
356
357        # remove temp dir; this will remove the temp file as well if it has not been renamed (e.g. for replaygain)
358        if temp_dir and os.path.exists(temp_dir):
359            rmtree(temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)
360
361        # This will use stats from ebu_pass2 if available (from the main second pass),
362        # or fall back to ebu_pass1.
363        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.replaygain:
364            _logger.debug(
365                "ReplayGain tagging is enabled. Proceeding with tag calculation/application."
366            )
367            self._run_replaygain()
368        else:
369            # Strip any existing ReplayGain tags from the output file
370            # since they are no longer accurate after normalization
371            self._strip_replaygain_tags(self.output_file)
372            # Copy input timestamps last, after any tag modifications, so the
373            # output ends up with the original modification time.
374            if self.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_mtime and not self.ffmpeg_normalize.dry_run:
375                self._apply_input_timestamps()
376            _logger.info(f"Normalized file written to {self.output_file}")
