class AudioStream(ffmpeg_normalize.MediaStream): 
148class AudioStream(MediaStream):
149    def __init__(
150        self,
151        ffmpeg_normalize: FFmpegNormalize,
152        media_file: MediaFile,
153        stream_id: int,
154        sample_rate: int | None,
155        bit_depth: int | None,
156        duration: float | None,
157        is_default: bool = False,
158        is_float: bool = False,
159    ):
160        """
161        Create an AudioStream object.
162
163        Args:
164            ffmpeg_normalize (FFmpegNormalize): The FFmpegNormalize object.
165            media_file (MediaFile): The MediaFile object.
166            stream_id (int): The stream ID.
167            sample_rate (int): sample rate in Hz
168            bit_depth (int): bit depth in bits
169            duration (float): duration in seconds
170            is_default (bool): Whether this stream has the default disposition flag
171            is_float (bool): Whether the stream uses a floating-point sample format
172        """
173        super().__init__(ffmpeg_normalize, media_file, "audio", stream_id)
174
175        self.loudness_statistics: LoudnessStatistics = {
176            "ebu_pass1": None,
177            "ebu_pass2": None,
178            "mean": None,
179            "max": None,
180        }
181
182        # Gain in dB applied by the second pass volume filter (peak/RMS), or 0
183        # when normalization is skipped for this stream (e.g. with lower_only).
184        # Stays None for EBU, where the gain is derived from the second pass stats.
185        self.applied_gain: float | None = None
186        self.verification_target_level: float | None = None
187        self.verification: VerificationResult | None = None
188
189        self.sample_rate = sample_rate
190        self.bit_depth = bit_depth
191
192        self.duration = duration
193        self.is_default = is_default
194        self.is_float = is_float
195
196    @staticmethod
197    def _constrain(
198        number: float, min_range: float, max_range: float, name: str | None = None
199    ) -> float:
200        """
201        Constrain a number between two values.
202
203        Args:
204            number (float): The number to constrain.
205            min_range (float): The minimum value.
206            max_range (float): The maximum value.
207            name (str): The name of the number (for logging).
208
209        Returns:
210            float: The constrained number.
211
212        Raises:
213            ValueError: If min_range is greater than max_range.
214        """
215        if min_range > max_range:
216            raise ValueError("min must be smaller than max")
217        result = max(min(number, max_range), min_range)
218        if result != number and name is not None:
219            _logger.warning(
220                f"Constraining {name} to range of [{min_range}, {max_range}]: {number} -> {result}"
221            )
222        return result
223
224    def get_stats(self) -> LoudnessStatisticsWithMetadata:
225        """
226        Return loudness statistics for the stream.
227
228        Returns:
229            dict: A dictionary containing the loudness statistics.
230        """
231        stats: LoudnessStatisticsWithMetadata = {
232            "input_file": self.media_file.input_file,
233            "output_file": self.media_file.output_file,
234            "stream_id": self.stream_id,
235            "ebu_pass1": self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"],
236            "ebu_pass2": self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass2"],
237            "mean": self.loudness_statistics["mean"],
238            "max": self.loudness_statistics["max"],
239            "status": self.media_file.status,
240        }
241        if self.verification is not None:
242            stats["verification"] = self.verification
243        # Only present when the file failed to process, per the per-file outcome
244        # reporting (status is "error").
245        if self.media_file.error is not None:
246            stats["error"] = self.media_file.error
247        return stats
248
249    def get_summary(self) -> SummaryRow:
250        """
251        Return the before/after levels and the applied gain for the stream.
252
253        For EBU, the input level and true peak come from the first pass (or the
254        second pass in dynamic mode), and the output level, output true peak and
255        gain come from the second pass. For RMS and peak, the input level is the
256        measured RMS or peak level, and the output values are computed from the
257        applied gain. Values that are not available are None. The output_source
258        field labels these values; verification, when present, contains separate
259        measurements of the encoded output and the check results.
260
261        Returns:
262            dict: A dictionary with the summary values.
263        """
264        normalization_type = self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type
265        status = self.media_file.status
266
267        input_level: float | None = None
268        input_peak: float | None = None
269        output_level: float | None = None
270        output_peak: float | None = None
271        gain: float | None = None
272
273        if normalization_type == "ebu":
274            pass1 = self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]
275            pass2 = self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass2"]
276            input_stats = pass1 if pass1 is not None else pass2
277            if input_stats is not None:
278                input_level = float(input_stats["input_i"])
279                input_peak = float(input_stats["input_tp"])
280            if pass2 is not None:
281                output_level = float(pass2["output_i"])
282                output_peak = float(pass2["output_tp"])
283                # Input and output of the same pass, as the first pass input
284                # measurement can differ slightly from the second pass one
285                gain = output_level - float(pass2["input_i"])
286        else:
287            measured = (
288                self.loudness_statistics["mean"]
289                if normalization_type == "rms"
290                else self.loudness_statistics["max"]
291            )
292            if measured is not None:
293                input_level = float(measured)
294            if self.loudness_statistics["max"] is not None:
295                input_peak = float(self.loudness_statistics["max"])
296
297        applied_gain = 0.0 if status == "skipped" else self.applied_gain
298        if (
299            status != "error"
300            and output_level is None
301            and applied_gain is not None
302            and input_level is not None
303        ):
304            gain = applied_gain
305            output_level = input_level + applied_gain
306            if input_peak is not None:
307                output_peak = input_peak + applied_gain
308
309        if status == "error":
310            output_level = output_peak = gain = None
311
312        source = "unavailable"
313        if output_level is not None:
314            source = (
315                "input"
316                if status == "skipped"
317                else (
318                    "filter"
319                    if normalization_type == "ebu"
320                    and self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass2"] is not None
321                    else "calculated"
322                )
323            )
324        summary: SummaryRow = {
325            "input_file": self.media_file.input_file,
326            "output_file": self.media_file.output_file,
327            "stream_id": self.stream_id,
328            "status": status,
329            "input_level": input_level,
330            "output_level": output_level,
331            "output_peak": output_peak,
332            "gain": gain,
333            "output_source": source,
334        }
335        if self.verification is not None:
336            summary["verification"] = self.verification
337        return summary
338
339    def set_second_pass_stats(self, stats: EbuLoudnessStatistics) -> None:
340        """
341        Set the EBU loudness statistics for the second pass.
342
343        Args:
344            stats (dict): The EBU loudness statistics.
345        """
346        _logger.debug(
347            f"Setting second pass stats for stream {self.stream_id} from {stats}"
348        )
349        self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass2"] = stats
350
351    def get_pcm_codec(self) -> str:
352        """
353        Get the PCM codec string for the stream.
354
355        Returns:
356            str: The PCM codec string.
357        """
358        if not self.bit_depth:
359            return "pcm_s16le"
360        elif self.bit_depth <= 8:
361            return "pcm_s8"
362        elif self.bit_depth in [16, 24, 32, 64]:
363            return f"pcm_s{self.bit_depth}le"
364        else:
365            _logger.warning(
366                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Unsupported bit depth {self.bit_depth}, falling back to pcm_s16le"
367            )
368            return "pcm_s16le"
369
370    def get_output_sample_fmt(self, codec: str | None) -> str | None:
371        """
372        Choose an output sample format for the given encoder that preserves the
373        detected input bit depth as closely as possible.
374
375        Used by the ``keep_bit_depth`` option (enabled by default) so that
376        encoders such as FLAC, which would otherwise pick their own default
377        sample format, retain the input bit depth. Only integer formats are
378        considered, and floating-point sources are left to the encoder, since
379        keeping bit depth is only meaningful for integer PCM sources.
380
381        Note that ffmpeg has no 24-bit sample format; 24-bit audio is carried in
382        the 32-bit ``s32`` format, and the encoder stores it accordingly.
383
384        Args:
385            codec: The output audio codec name, or None for the PCM default.
386
387        Returns:
388            str | None: The chosen sample format, or None if none should be set
389                (unknown bit depth, floating-point source, no explicit codec, no
390                encoder info, or an encoder without integer sample formats). In
391                all of these cases the encoder default is used.
392        """
393        if not self.bit_depth:
394            _logger.debug(
395                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Could not determine input bit depth "
396                f"for stream {self.stream_id}; leaving the sample format to the encoder."
397            )
398            return None
399
400        if self.is_float:
401            # Pinning an integer sample format would silently convert a
402            # floating-point source to integer, so leave it to the encoder.
403            _logger.debug(
404                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Stream {self.stream_id} is "
405                "floating-point; leaving the sample format to the encoder."
406            )
407            return None
408
409        if codec is None:
410            # The PCM default path already derives the bit depth from the input
411            # via get_pcm_codec(), so there is nothing to set here.
412            _logger.debug(
413                "keep_bit_depth has no effect for the default PCM output; the "
414                "input bit depth is already preserved."
415            )
416            return None
417
418        supported = get_encoder_sample_formats(codec)
419        if not supported:
420            _logger.debug(
421                f"Could not determine supported sample formats for codec '{codec}'; "
422                "not setting an explicit sample format."
423            )
424            return None
425
426        # Only consider integer formats, since keeping bit depth is meaningful
427        # for integer PCM sources (e.g. FLAC, ALAC).
428        int_formats = [
429            fmt
430            for fmt in supported
431            if fmt in _SAMPLE_FMT_INFO and not _SAMPLE_FMT_INFO[fmt][1]
432        ]
433        if not int_formats:
434            _logger.debug(
435                f"Encoder '{codec}' supports no integer sample formats; "
436                "leaving the sample format to the encoder."
437            )
438            return None
439
440        # Prefer the smallest integer format that holds at least the input bit
441        # depth; fall back to the largest available if none is big enough.
442        candidates = sorted(int_formats, key=lambda fmt: _SAMPLE_FMT_INFO[fmt][0])
443        for fmt in candidates:
444            if _SAMPLE_FMT_INFO[fmt][0] >= self.bit_depth:
445                return fmt
446        return candidates[-1]
447
448    def _get_filter_str_with_pre_filter(self, current_filter: str) -> str:
449        """
450        Get a filter string for current_filter, with the pre-filter
451        added before. Applies the input label before.
452
453        If a target channel count is set via ``audio_channels``, a channel
454        layout conversion is inserted before the analysis/normalization
455        filter so that measurements reflect the downmixed signal.
456
457        Args:
458            current_filter (str): The current filter.
459
460        Returns:
461            str: The filter string.
462        """
463        input_label = f"[0:{self.stream_id}]"
464        filter_chain = []
465        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.pre_filter:
466            filter_chain.append(self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.pre_filter)
467        channel_conversion = self._get_channel_conversion_filter()
468        if channel_conversion:
469            filter_chain.append(channel_conversion)
470        filter_chain.append(current_filter)
471        filter_str = input_label + ",".join(filter_chain)
472        return filter_str
473
474    def _get_channel_conversion_filter(self) -> str | None:
475        """
476        Return an ``aformat`` filter string that downmixes/upmixes to the
477        requested channel count, or None if no conversion is configured.
478
479        The ``Nc`` channel-layout notation matches ffmpeg's default layout
480        selection for ``-ac N``, so the analysis pass measures the same
481        signal that the output will contain.
482
483        A float planar sample format is requested so the downmix is not
484        attenuated to fit an integer range. This is what the analysis
485        measurement should reflect, since the volume gain is applied in
486        the filter graph (where samples are also float) before being
487        written to the output codec.
488        """
489        audio_channels = self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.audio_channels
490        if not audio_channels:
491            return None
492        return f"aformat=sample_fmts=fltp:channel_layouts={audio_channels}c"
493
494    def parse_astats(self) -> Iterator[float]:
495        """
496        Use ffmpeg with astats filter to get the mean (RMS) and max (peak) volume of the input file.
497
498        Yields:
499            float: The progress of the command.
500        """
501        _logger.info(f"Running first pass astats filter for stream {self.stream_id}")
502
503        filter_str = self._get_filter_str_with_pre_filter(
504            "astats=measure_overall=Peak_level+RMS_level:measure_perchannel=0"
505        )
506
507        cmd = [
508            self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.ffmpeg_exe,
509            "-hide_banner",
510            "-y",
511        ]
512
513        # Add extra input options if specified
514        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_input_options:
515            cmd.extend(self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_input_options)
516
517        cmd.extend(
518            [
519                "-i",
520                self.media_file.input_file,
521                "-filter_complex",
522                filter_str,
523                "-vn",
524                "-sn",
525                "-f",
526                "null",
527                os.devnull,
528            ]
529        )
530
531        cmd_runner = CommandRunner()
532        yield from cmd_runner.run_ffmpeg_command(cmd)
533        output = cmd_runner.get_output()
534
535        _logger.debug(
536            f"astats command output: {CommandRunner.prune_ffmpeg_progress_from_output(output)}"
537        )
538
539        mean_volume_matches = re.findall(r"RMS level dB: ([\-\d\.]+)", output)
540        if mean_volume_matches:
541            if mean_volume_matches[0] == "-":
542                self.loudness_statistics["mean"] = float("-inf")
543            else:
544                self.loudness_statistics["mean"] = float(mean_volume_matches[0])
545        else:
546            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
547                f"Could not get mean volume for {self.media_file.input_file}"
548            )
549
550        max_volume_matches = re.findall(r"Peak level dB: ([\-\d\.]+)", output)
551        if max_volume_matches:
552            if max_volume_matches[0] == "-":
553                self.loudness_statistics["max"] = float("-inf")
554            else:
555                self.loudness_statistics["max"] = float(max_volume_matches[0])
556        else:
557            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
558                f"Could not get max volume for {self.media_file.input_file}"
559            )
560
561    def parse_loudnorm_stats(self) -> Iterator[float]:
562        """
563        Run a first pass loudnorm filter to get measured data.
564
565        Yields:
566            float: The progress of the command.
567        """
568        _logger.info(f"Running first pass loudnorm filter for stream {self.stream_id}")
569
570        opts = {
571            "i": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level,
572            "lra": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target,
573            "tp": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak,
574            "offset": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.offset,
575            "print_format": "json",
576        }
577
578        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dual_mono:
579            opts["dual_mono"] = "true"
580
581        filter_str = self._get_filter_str_with_pre_filter(
582            "loudnorm=" + dict_to_filter_opts(opts)
583        )
584
585        cmd = [
586            self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.ffmpeg_exe,
587            "-hide_banner",
588            "-y",
589        ]
590
591        # Add extra input options if specified
592        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_input_options:
593            cmd.extend(self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_input_options)
594
595        cmd.extend(
596            [
597                "-i",
598                self.media_file.input_file,
599                "-map",
600                f"0:{self.stream_id}",
601                "-filter_complex",
602                filter_str,
603                "-vn",
604                "-sn",
605                "-f",
606                "null",
607                os.devnull,
608            ]
609        )
610
611        cmd_runner = CommandRunner()
612        yield from cmd_runner.run_ffmpeg_command(cmd)
613        output = cmd_runner.get_output()
614
615        _logger.debug(
616            f"Loudnorm first pass command output: {CommandRunner.prune_ffmpeg_progress_from_output(output)}"
617        )
618
619        # only one stream
620        self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"] = next(
621            iter(AudioStream.prune_and_parse_loudnorm_output(output).values())
622        )
623
624    @staticmethod
625    def prune_and_parse_loudnorm_output(
626        output: str,
627    ) -> dict[int, EbuLoudnessStatistics]:
628        """
629        Prune ffmpeg progress lines from output and parse the loudnorm filter output.
630        There may be multiple outputs if multiple streams were processed.
631
632        Args:
633            output (str): The output from ffmpeg.
634
635        Returns:
636            dict[int, EbuLoudnessStatistics]: The EBU loudness statistics.
637        """
638        _logger.debug("Parsing loudnorm stats from output")
639        pruned_output = CommandRunner.prune_ffmpeg_progress_from_output(output)
640        output_lines = [line.strip() for line in pruned_output.split("\n")]
641        return AudioStream._parse_loudnorm_output(output_lines)
642
643    @staticmethod
644    def _parse_loudnorm_output(
645        output_lines: list[str],
646    ) -> dict[int, EbuLoudnessStatistics]:
647        """
648        Parse the output of a loudnorm filter to get the EBU loudness statistics.
649
650        Args:
651            output_lines (list[str]): The output lines of the loudnorm filter.
652
653        Raises:
654            FFmpegNormalizeError: When the output could not be parsed.
655
656        Returns:
657            dict[int, EbuLoudnessStatistics]: stream index and the EBU loudness statistics, if found.
658        """
659        result = dict[int, EbuLoudnessStatistics]()
660        stream_index = -1
661        loudnorm_start = 0
662        for index, line in enumerate(output_lines):
663            if stream_index < 0:
664                if m := _loudnorm_pattern.match(line):
665                    loudnorm_start = index + 1
666                    stream_index = int(m.group(1))
667            else:
668                if line.startswith("}"):
669                    loudnorm_end = index + 1
670                    loudnorm_data = "\n".join(output_lines[loudnorm_start:loudnorm_end])
671
672                    try:
673                        loudnorm_stats = json.loads(loudnorm_data)
674
675                        _logger.debug(
676                            f"Loudnorm stats for stream {stream_index} parsed: {loudnorm_data}"
677                        )
678
679                        for key in [
680                            "input_i",
681                            "input_tp",
682                            "input_lra",
683                            "input_thresh",
684                            "output_i",
685                            "output_tp",
686                            "output_lra",
687                            "output_thresh",
688                            "target_offset",
689                            "normalization_type",
690                        ]:
691                            if key not in loudnorm_stats:
692                                continue
693                            if key == "normalization_type":
694                                loudnorm_stats[key] = loudnorm_stats[key].lower()
695                            # handle infinite values
696                            elif float(loudnorm_stats[key]) == -float("inf"):
697                                loudnorm_stats[key] = -99
698                            elif float(loudnorm_stats[key]) == float("inf"):
699                                loudnorm_stats[key] = 0
700                            else:
701                                # convert to floats
702                                loudnorm_stats[key] = float(loudnorm_stats[key])
703
704                        result[stream_index] = cast(
705                            EbuLoudnessStatistics, loudnorm_stats
706                        )
707                        stream_index = -1
708                    except Exception as e:
709                        raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
710                            f"Could not parse loudnorm stats; wrong JSON format in string: {e}"
711                        )
712        return result
713
714    def get_second_pass_opts_ebu(self, batch_reference: float | None = None) -> str:
715        """
716        Return second pass loudnorm filter options string for ffmpeg
717
718        Args:
719            batch_reference (float | None, optional): Reference loudness for batch mode.
720                When provided, the target level is adjusted to preserve relative loudness.
721                Defaults to None.
722        """
723
724        # In dynamic mode, we can do everything in one pass, and we do not have first pass stats
725        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dynamic:
726            if not self.ffmpeg_normalize.sample_rate:
727                _logger.warning(
728                    "In dynamic mode, the sample rate will automatically be set to 192 kHz by the loudnorm filter. "
729                    "Specify -ar/--sample-rate to override it."
730                )
731
732            opts = {
733                "i": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level,
734                "lra": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target,
735                "tp": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak,
736                "offset": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.offset,
737                "linear": "false",
738                "print_format": "json",
739            }
740
741            if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dual_mono:
742                opts["dual_mono"] = "true"
743
744            self.verification_target_level = float(opts["i"])
745            return "loudnorm=" + dict_to_filter_opts(opts)
746
747        if not self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]:
748            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
749                "First pass not run, you must call parse_loudnorm_stats first"
750            )
751
752        if float(self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_i"]) > 0:
753            _logger.warning(
754                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Input file had measured input loudness greater than zero "
755                f"({self.loudness_statistics['ebu_pass1']['input_i']}), capping at 0"
756            )
757            self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_i"] = 0
758
759        will_use_dynamic_mode: bool = self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dynamic
760
761        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_loudness_range_target:
762            _logger.debug(
763                "Keeping target loudness range in second pass loudnorm filter"
764            )
765            input_lra = self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_lra"]
766            if input_lra < 1 or input_lra > 50:
767                _logger.warning(
768                    f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Input file had measured loudness range outside of [1,50] "
769                    f"({input_lra}), capping to allowed range"
770                )
771
772            self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target = self._constrain(
773                self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_lra"], 1, 50
774            )
775
776        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_lra_above_loudness_range_target:
777            if (
778                self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_lra"]
779                <= self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target
780            ):
781                _logger.debug(
782                    "Setting loudness range target in second pass loudnorm filter"
783                )
784            else:
785                self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target = (
786                    self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_lra"]
787                )
788                _logger.debug(
789                    "Keeping target loudness range in second pass loudnorm filter"
790                )
791
792        if (
793            self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target
794            < self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_lra"]
795            and not will_use_dynamic_mode
796        ):
797            _logger.warning(
798                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Input file had loudness range of {self.loudness_statistics['ebu_pass1']['input_lra']}. "
799                f"This is larger than the loudness range target ({self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target}). "
800                "Normalization will revert to dynamic mode. Choose a higher target loudness range if you want linear normalization. "
801                "Alternatively, use the --keep-loudness-range-target or --keep-lra-above-loudness-range-target option to keep the target loudness range from "
802                "the input."
803            )
804            will_use_dynamic_mode = True
805
806        if will_use_dynamic_mode and not self.ffmpeg_normalize.sample_rate:
807            _logger.warning(
808                "In dynamic mode, the sample rate will automatically be set to 192 kHz by the loudnorm filter. "
809                "Specify -ar/--sample-rate to override it."
810            )
811
812        target_level = self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level
813        target_offset = self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["target_offset"]
814        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.auto_lower_loudness_target:
815            safe_target = (
816                self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_i"]
817                - self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_tp"]
818                + self.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak
819                - 0.1
820            )
821            if safe_target < self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level:
822                target_level = safe_target
823                # The first-pass correction belongs to the original target.
824                # Reusing it at the lowered target adds unwanted gain when
825                # loudnorm falls back to dynamic mode (e.g. for zero LRA).
826                target_offset = 0.0
827                _logger.warning(
828                    f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Using loudness target {target_level:.2f} because --auto-lower-loudness-target given.",
829                )
830
831        stats = self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]
832
833        # Check if the true peak constraint will force dynamic mode.
834        # In linear mode, a uniform gain of (target - input_i) is applied.
835        # If that would leave the true peak above the TP limit, loudnorm
836        # cannot satisfy both constraints linearly and will fall back to
837        # dynamic processing.
838        if not will_use_dynamic_mode:
839            linear_gain = target_level - stats["input_i"]
840            estimated_tp = stats["input_tp"] + linear_gain
841            if estimated_tp > self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak:
842                min_tp = estimated_tp
843                max_target = (
844                    self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak
845                    - stats["input_tp"]
846                    + stats["input_i"]
847                )
848                _logger.warning(
849                    f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Linear normalization would result in an estimated true peak of "
850                    f"{estimated_tp:.2f} dBTP (input true peak {stats['input_tp']:.2f} dBTP + gain of {linear_gain:.2f} dB), "
851                    f"which exceeds the target true peak of {self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak} dBTP. "
852                    "The loudnorm filter will likely use dynamic mode instead. "
853                    f"To avoid this, raise --true-peak (-tp) to at least {min_tp:.1f}, "
854                    f"or lower the target level (-t) to at most {max_target:.1f}."
855                )
856
857        # Adjust target level for batch mode to preserve relative loudness
858        if batch_reference is not None:
859            input_i = float(stats["input_i"])
860            # Formula: adjusted_target = target_level + (input_i - batch_reference)
861            # If track is quieter than average (input_i < batch_ref), offset is negative → quieter target
862            # If track is louder than average (input_i > batch_ref), offset is positive → louder target
863            adjusted_target = target_level + (input_i - batch_reference)
864            _logger.info(
865                f"Batch mode: Adjusting target from {target_level:.2f} to {adjusted_target:.2f} LUFS "
866                f"(input_i={input_i:.2f}, batch_ref={batch_reference:.2f}, offset={input_i - batch_reference:.2f})"
867            )
868            target_level = adjusted_target
869
870        opts = {
871            "i": target_level,
872            "lra": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target,
873            "tp": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak,
874            "offset": self._constrain(target_offset, -99, 99, name="target_offset"),
875            "measured_i": self._constrain(stats["input_i"], -99, 0, name="input_i"),
876            "measured_lra": self._constrain(
877                stats["input_lra"], 0, 99, name="input_lra"
878            ),
879            "measured_tp": self._constrain(stats["input_tp"], -99, 99, name="input_tp"),
880            "measured_thresh": self._constrain(
881                stats["input_thresh"], -99, 0, name="input_thresh"
882            ),
883            "linear": "false" if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dynamic else "true",
884            "print_format": "json",
885        }
886
887        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dual_mono:
888            opts["dual_mono"] = "true"
889
890        self.verification_target_level = target_level
891        return "loudnorm=" + dict_to_filter_opts(opts)
892
893    def get_second_pass_opts_peakrms(self, batch_reference: float | None = None) -> str:
894        """
895        Set the adjustment gain based on chosen option and mean/max volume,
896        return the matching ffmpeg volume filter.
897
898        Args:
899            batch_reference (float | None, optional): Reference loudness for batch mode.
900                When provided, the target level is adjusted to preserve relative loudness.
901                Defaults to None.
902
903        Returns:
904            str: ffmpeg volume filter string
905        """
906        if (
907            self.loudness_statistics["max"] is None
908            or self.loudness_statistics["mean"] is None
909        ):
910            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
911                "First pass not run, no mean/max volume to normalize to"
912            )
913
914        normalization_type = self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type
915        target_level = self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level
916
917        # Adjust target level for batch mode to preserve relative loudness
918        if batch_reference is not None:
919            if normalization_type == "peak":
920                measured_level = float(self.loudness_statistics["max"])
921            elif normalization_type == "rms":
922                measured_level = float(self.loudness_statistics["mean"])
923            else:
924                raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
925                    "Can only set adjustment for peak and RMS normalization"
926                )
927
928            # Formula: adjusted_target = target_level + (measured_level - batch_reference)
929            # If track is quieter than average (measured < batch_ref), offset is negative → quieter target
930            # If track is louder than average (measured > batch_ref), offset is positive → louder target
931            adjusted_target = target_level + (measured_level - batch_reference)
932            _logger.info(
933                f"Batch mode: Adjusting target from {target_level:.2f} to {adjusted_target:.2f} dB "
934                f"(measured={measured_level:.2f}, batch_ref={batch_reference:.2f}, offset={measured_level - batch_reference:.2f})"
935            )
936            target_level = adjusted_target
937
938        if normalization_type == "peak":
939            adjustment = 0 + target_level - self.loudness_statistics["max"]
940        elif normalization_type == "rms":
941            adjustment = target_level - self.loudness_statistics["mean"]
942        else:
943            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
944                "Can only set adjustment for peak and RMS normalization"
945            )
946
947        _logger.info(
948            f"Adjusting stream {self.stream_id} by {adjustment} dB to reach {target_level}"
949        )
950
951        self.applied_gain = float(adjustment)
952
953        clip_amount = self.loudness_statistics["max"] + adjustment
954        if clip_amount > 0:
955            _logger.warning(
956                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Adjusting will lead to clipping of {clip_amount} dB"
957            )
958
959        return f"volume={adjustment}dB"

def get_stats(self) -> ffmpeg_normalize._streams.LoudnessStatisticsWithMetadata: 
224    def get_stats(self) -> LoudnessStatisticsWithMetadata:
225        """
226        Return loudness statistics for the stream.
227
228        Returns:
229            dict: A dictionary containing the loudness statistics.
230        """
231        stats: LoudnessStatisticsWithMetadata = {
232            "input_file": self.media_file.input_file,
233            "output_file": self.media_file.output_file,
234            "stream_id": self.stream_id,
235            "ebu_pass1": self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"],
236            "ebu_pass2": self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass2"],
237            "mean": self.loudness_statistics["mean"],
238            "max": self.loudness_statistics["max"],
239            "status": self.media_file.status,
240        }
241        if self.verification is not None:
242            stats["verification"] = self.verification
243        # Only present when the file failed to process, per the per-file outcome
244        # reporting (status is "error").
245        if self.media_file.error is not None:
246            stats["error"] = self.media_file.error
247        return stats

Return loudness statistics for the stream.

Returns:

dict: A dictionary containing the loudness statistics.

def get_summary(self) -> ffmpeg_normalize._streams.SummaryRow: 
249    def get_summary(self) -> SummaryRow:
250        """
251        Return the before/after levels and the applied gain for the stream.
252
253        For EBU, the input level and true peak come from the first pass (or the
254        second pass in dynamic mode), and the output level, output true peak and
255        gain come from the second pass. For RMS and peak, the input level is the
256        measured RMS or peak level, and the output values are computed from the
257        applied gain. Values that are not available are None. The output_source
258        field labels these values; verification, when present, contains separate
259        measurements of the encoded output and the check results.
260
261        Returns:
262            dict: A dictionary with the summary values.
263        """
264        normalization_type = self.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type
265        status = self.media_file.status
266
267        input_level: float | None = None
268        input_peak: float | None = None
269        output_level: float | None = None
270        output_peak: float | None = None
271        gain: float | None = None
272
273        if normalization_type == "ebu":
274            pass1 = self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]
275            pass2 = self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass2"]
276            input_stats = pass1 if pass1 is not None else pass2
277            if input_stats is not None:
278                input_level = float(input_stats["input_i"])
279                input_peak = float(input_stats["input_tp"])
280            if pass2 is not None:
281                output_level = float(pass2["output_i"])
282                output_peak = float(pass2["output_tp"])
283                # Input and output of the same pass, as the first pass input
284                # measurement can differ slightly from the second pass one
285                gain = output_level - float(pass2["input_i"])
286        else:
287            measured = (
288                self.loudness_statistics["mean"]
289                if normalization_type == "rms"
290                else self.loudness_statistics["max"]
291            )
292            if measured is not None:
293                input_level = float(measured)
294            if self.loudness_statistics["max"] is not None:
295                input_peak = float(self.loudness_statistics["max"])
296
297        applied_gain = 0.0 if status == "skipped" else self.applied_gain
298        if (
299            status != "error"
300            and output_level is None
301            and applied_gain is not None
302            and input_level is not None
303        ):
304            gain = applied_gain
305            output_level = input_level + applied_gain
306            if input_peak is not None:
307                output_peak = input_peak + applied_gain
308
309        if status == "error":
310            output_level = output_peak = gain = None
311
312        source = "unavailable"
313        if output_level is not None:
314            source = (
315                "input"
316                if status == "skipped"
317                else (
318                    "filter"
319                    if normalization_type == "ebu"
320                    and self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass2"] is not None
321                    else "calculated"
322                )
323            )
324        summary: SummaryRow = {
325            "input_file": self.media_file.input_file,
326            "output_file": self.media_file.output_file,
327            "stream_id": self.stream_id,
328            "status": status,
329            "input_level": input_level,
330            "output_level": output_level,
331            "output_peak": output_peak,
332            "gain": gain,
333            "output_source": source,
334        }
335        if self.verification is not None:
336            summary["verification"] = self.verification
337        return summary

Return the before/after levels and the applied gain for the stream.

For EBU, the input level and true peak come from the first pass (or the second pass in dynamic mode), and the output level, output true peak and gain come from the second pass. For RMS and peak, the input level is the measured RMS or peak level, and the output values are computed from the applied gain. Values that are not available are None. The output_source field labels these values; verification, when present, contains separate measurements of the encoded output and the check results.

Returns:

dict: A dictionary with the summary values.

def get_pcm_codec(self) -> str: 
351    def get_pcm_codec(self) -> str:
352        """
353        Get the PCM codec string for the stream.
354
355        Returns:
356            str: The PCM codec string.
357        """
358        if not self.bit_depth:
359            return "pcm_s16le"
360        elif self.bit_depth <= 8:
361            return "pcm_s8"
362        elif self.bit_depth in [16, 24, 32, 64]:
363            return f"pcm_s{self.bit_depth}le"
364        else:
365            _logger.warning(
366                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Unsupported bit depth {self.bit_depth}, falling back to pcm_s16le"
367            )
368            return "pcm_s16le"

str: The PCM codec string.

def get_output_sample_fmt(self, codec: str | None) -> str | None: 
370    def get_output_sample_fmt(self, codec: str | None) -> str | None:
371        """
372        Choose an output sample format for the given encoder that preserves the
373        detected input bit depth as closely as possible.
374
375        Used by the ``keep_bit_depth`` option (enabled by default) so that
376        encoders such as FLAC, which would otherwise pick their own default
377        sample format, retain the input bit depth. Only integer formats are
378        considered, and floating-point sources are left to the encoder, since
379        keeping bit depth is only meaningful for integer PCM sources.
380
381        Note that ffmpeg has no 24-bit sample format; 24-bit audio is carried in
382        the 32-bit ``s32`` format, and the encoder stores it accordingly.
383
384        Args:
385            codec: The output audio codec name, or None for the PCM default.
386
387        Returns:
388            str | None: The chosen sample format, or None if none should be set
389                (unknown bit depth, floating-point source, no explicit codec, no
390                encoder info, or an encoder without integer sample formats). In
391                all of these cases the encoder default is used.
392        """
393        if not self.bit_depth:
394            _logger.debug(
395                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Could not determine input bit depth "
396                f"for stream {self.stream_id}; leaving the sample format to the encoder."
397            )
398            return None
399
400        if self.is_float:
401            # Pinning an integer sample format would silently convert a
402            # floating-point source to integer, so leave it to the encoder.
403            _logger.debug(
404                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Stream {self.stream_id} is "
405                "floating-point; leaving the sample format to the encoder."
406            )
407            return None
408
409        if codec is None:
410            # The PCM default path already derives the bit depth from the input
411            # via get_pcm_codec(), so there is nothing to set here.
412            _logger.debug(
413                "keep_bit_depth has no effect for the default PCM output; the "
414                "input bit depth is already preserved."
415            )
416            return None
417
418        supported = get_encoder_sample_formats(codec)
419        if not supported:
420            _logger.debug(
421                f"Could not determine supported sample formats for codec '{codec}'; "
422                "not setting an explicit sample format."
423            )
424            return None
425
426        # Only consider integer formats, since keeping bit depth is meaningful
427        # for integer PCM sources (e.g. FLAC, ALAC).
428        int_formats = [
429            fmt
430            for fmt in supported
431            if fmt in _SAMPLE_FMT_INFO and not _SAMPLE_FMT_INFO[fmt][1]
432        ]
433        if not int_formats:
434            _logger.debug(
435                f"Encoder '{codec}' supports no integer sample formats; "
436                "leaving the sample format to the encoder."
437            )
438            return None
439
440        # Prefer the smallest integer format that holds at least the input bit
441        # depth; fall back to the largest available if none is big enough.
442        candidates = sorted(int_formats, key=lambda fmt: _SAMPLE_FMT_INFO[fmt][0])
443        for fmt in candidates:
444            if _SAMPLE_FMT_INFO[fmt][0] >= self.bit_depth:
445                return fmt
446        return candidates[-1]

Choose an output sample format for the given encoder that preserves the detected input bit depth as closely as possible.

Used by the keep_bit_depth option (enabled by default) so that encoders such as FLAC, which would otherwise pick their own default sample format, retain the input bit depth. Only integer formats are considered, and floating-point sources are left to the encoder, since keeping bit depth is only meaningful for integer PCM sources.

Note that ffmpeg has no 24-bit sample format; 24-bit audio is carried in the 32-bit s32 format, and the encoder stores it accordingly.

Arguments:
  • codec: The output audio codec name, or None for the PCM default.
Returns:

str | None: The chosen sample format, or None if none should be set (unknown bit depth, floating-point source, no explicit codec, no encoder info, or an encoder without integer sample formats). In all of these cases the encoder default is used.

def parse_astats(self) -> Iterator[float]: 
494    def parse_astats(self) -> Iterator[float]:
495        """
496        Use ffmpeg with astats filter to get the mean (RMS) and max (peak) volume of the input file.
497
498        Yields:
499            float: The progress of the command.
500        """
501        _logger.info(f"Running first pass astats filter for stream {self.stream_id}")
502
503        filter_str = self._get_filter_str_with_pre_filter(
504            "astats=measure_overall=Peak_level+RMS_level:measure_perchannel=0"
505        )
506
507        cmd = [
508            self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.ffmpeg_exe,
509            "-hide_banner",
510            "-y",
511        ]
512
513        # Add extra input options if specified
514        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_input_options:
515            cmd.extend(self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_input_options)
516
517        cmd.extend(
518            [
519                "-i",
520                self.media_file.input_file,
521                "-filter_complex",
522                filter_str,
523                "-vn",
524                "-sn",
525                "-f",
526                "null",
527                os.devnull,
528            ]
529        )
530
531        cmd_runner = CommandRunner()
532        yield from cmd_runner.run_ffmpeg_command(cmd)
533        output = cmd_runner.get_output()
534
535        _logger.debug(
536            f"astats command output: {CommandRunner.prune_ffmpeg_progress_from_output(output)}"
537        )
538
539        mean_volume_matches = re.findall(r"RMS level dB: ([\-\d\.]+)", output)
540        if mean_volume_matches:
541            if mean_volume_matches[0] == "-":
542                self.loudness_statistics["mean"] = float("-inf")
543            else:
544                self.loudness_statistics["mean"] = float(mean_volume_matches[0])
545        else:
546            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
547                f"Could not get mean volume for {self.media_file.input_file}"
548            )
549
550        max_volume_matches = re.findall(r"Peak level dB: ([\-\d\.]+)", output)
551        if max_volume_matches:
552            if max_volume_matches[0] == "-":
553                self.loudness_statistics["max"] = float("-inf")
554            else:
555                self.loudness_statistics["max"] = float(max_volume_matches[0])
556        else:
557            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
558                f"Could not get max volume for {self.media_file.input_file}"
559            )

Use ffmpeg with astats filter to get the mean (RMS) and max (peak) volume of the input file.

Yields:

float: The progress of the command.

def parse_loudnorm_stats(self) -> Iterator[float]: 
561    def parse_loudnorm_stats(self) -> Iterator[float]:
562        """
563        Run a first pass loudnorm filter to get measured data.
564
565        Yields:
566            float: The progress of the command.
567        """
568        _logger.info(f"Running first pass loudnorm filter for stream {self.stream_id}")
569
570        opts = {
571            "i": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level,
572            "lra": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target,
573            "tp": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak,
574            "offset": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.offset,
575            "print_format": "json",
576        }
577
578        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dual_mono:
579            opts["dual_mono"] = "true"
580
581        filter_str = self._get_filter_str_with_pre_filter(
582            "loudnorm=" + dict_to_filter_opts(opts)
583        )
584
585        cmd = [
586            self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.ffmpeg_exe,
587            "-hide_banner",
588            "-y",
589        ]
590
591        # Add extra input options if specified
592        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_input_options:
593            cmd.extend(self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.extra_input_options)
594
595        cmd.extend(
596            [
597                "-i",
598                self.media_file.input_file,
599                "-map",
600                f"0:{self.stream_id}",
601                "-filter_complex",
602                filter_str,
603                "-vn",
604                "-sn",
605                "-f",
606                "null",
607                os.devnull,
608            ]
609        )
610
611        cmd_runner = CommandRunner()
612        yield from cmd_runner.run_ffmpeg_command(cmd)
613        output = cmd_runner.get_output()
614
615        _logger.debug(
616            f"Loudnorm first pass command output: {CommandRunner.prune_ffmpeg_progress_from_output(output)}"
617        )
618
619        # only one stream
620        self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"] = next(
621            iter(AudioStream.prune_and_parse_loudnorm_output(output).values())
622        )

Run a first pass loudnorm filter to get measured data.

Yields:

float: The progress of the command.

@staticmethod
def prune_and_parse_loudnorm_output( output: str) -> dict[int, ffmpeg_normalize._streams.EbuLoudnessStatistics]: 
624    @staticmethod
625    def prune_and_parse_loudnorm_output(
626        output: str,
627    ) -> dict[int, EbuLoudnessStatistics]:
628        """
629        Prune ffmpeg progress lines from output and parse the loudnorm filter output.
630        There may be multiple outputs if multiple streams were processed.
631
632        Args:
633            output (str): The output from ffmpeg.
634
635        Returns:
636            dict[int, EbuLoudnessStatistics]: The EBU loudness statistics.
637        """
638        _logger.debug("Parsing loudnorm stats from output")
639        pruned_output = CommandRunner.prune_ffmpeg_progress_from_output(output)
640        output_lines = [line.strip() for line in pruned_output.split("\n")]
641        return AudioStream._parse_loudnorm_output(output_lines)

def get_second_pass_opts_ebu(self, batch_reference: float | None = None) -> str: 
714    def get_second_pass_opts_ebu(self, batch_reference: float | None = None) -> str:
715        """
716        Return second pass loudnorm filter options string for ffmpeg
717
718        Args:
719            batch_reference (float | None, optional): Reference loudness for batch mode.
720                When provided, the target level is adjusted to preserve relative loudness.
721                Defaults to None.
722        """
723
724        # In dynamic mode, we can do everything in one pass, and we do not have first pass stats
725        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dynamic:
726            if not self.ffmpeg_normalize.sample_rate:
727                _logger.warning(
728                    "In dynamic mode, the sample rate will automatically be set to 192 kHz by the loudnorm filter. "
729                    "Specify -ar/--sample-rate to override it."
730                )
731
732            opts = {
733                "i": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level,
734                "lra": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target,
735                "tp": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak,
736                "offset": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.offset,
737                "linear": "false",
738                "print_format": "json",
739            }
740
741            if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dual_mono:
742                opts["dual_mono"] = "true"
743
744            self.verification_target_level = float(opts["i"])
745            return "loudnorm=" + dict_to_filter_opts(opts)
746
747        if not self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]:
748            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
749                "First pass not run, you must call parse_loudnorm_stats first"
750            )
751
752        if float(self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_i"]) > 0:
753            _logger.warning(
754                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Input file had measured input loudness greater than zero "
755                f"({self.loudness_statistics['ebu_pass1']['input_i']}), capping at 0"
756            )
757            self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_i"] = 0
758
759        will_use_dynamic_mode: bool = self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dynamic
760
761        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_loudness_range_target:
762            _logger.debug(
763                "Keeping target loudness range in second pass loudnorm filter"
764            )
765            input_lra = self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_lra"]
766            if input_lra < 1 or input_lra > 50:
767                _logger.warning(
768                    f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Input file had measured loudness range outside of [1,50] "
769                    f"({input_lra}), capping to allowed range"
770                )
771
772            self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target = self._constrain(
773                self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_lra"], 1, 50
774            )
775
776        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.keep_lra_above_loudness_range_target:
777            if (
778                self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_lra"]
779                <= self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target
780            ):
781                _logger.debug(
782                    "Setting loudness range target in second pass loudnorm filter"
783                )
784            else:
785                self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target = (
786                    self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_lra"]
787                )
788                _logger.debug(
789                    "Keeping target loudness range in second pass loudnorm filter"
790                )
791
792        if (
793            self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target
794            < self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_lra"]
795            and not will_use_dynamic_mode
796        ):
797            _logger.warning(
798                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Input file had loudness range of {self.loudness_statistics['ebu_pass1']['input_lra']}. "
799                f"This is larger than the loudness range target ({self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target}). "
800                "Normalization will revert to dynamic mode. Choose a higher target loudness range if you want linear normalization. "
801                "Alternatively, use the --keep-loudness-range-target or --keep-lra-above-loudness-range-target option to keep the target loudness range from "
802                "the input."
803            )
804            will_use_dynamic_mode = True
805
806        if will_use_dynamic_mode and not self.ffmpeg_normalize.sample_rate:
807            _logger.warning(
808                "In dynamic mode, the sample rate will automatically be set to 192 kHz by the loudnorm filter. "
809                "Specify -ar/--sample-rate to override it."
810            )
811
812        target_level = self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level
813        target_offset = self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["target_offset"]
814        if self.ffmpeg_normalize.auto_lower_loudness_target:
815            safe_target = (
816                self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_i"]
817                - self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]["input_tp"]
818                + self.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak
819                - 0.1
820            )
821            if safe_target < self.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level:
822                target_level = safe_target
823                # The first-pass correction belongs to the original target.
824                # Reusing it at the lowered target adds unwanted gain when
825                # loudnorm falls back to dynamic mode (e.g. for zero LRA).
826                target_offset = 0.0
827                _logger.warning(
828                    f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Using loudness target {target_level:.2f} because --auto-lower-loudness-target given.",
829                )
830
831        stats = self.loudness_statistics["ebu_pass1"]
832
833        # Check if the true peak constraint will force dynamic mode.
834        # In linear mode, a uniform gain of (target - input_i) is applied.
835        # If that would leave the true peak above the TP limit, loudnorm
836        # cannot satisfy both constraints linearly and will fall back to
837        # dynamic processing.
838        if not will_use_dynamic_mode:
839            linear_gain = target_level - stats["input_i"]
840            estimated_tp = stats["input_tp"] + linear_gain
841            if estimated_tp > self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak:
842                min_tp = estimated_tp
843                max_target = (
844                    self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak
845                    - stats["input_tp"]
846                    + stats["input_i"]
847                )
848                _logger.warning(
849                    f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Linear normalization would result in an estimated true peak of "
850                    f"{estimated_tp:.2f} dBTP (input true peak {stats['input_tp']:.2f} dBTP + gain of {linear_gain:.2f} dB), "
851                    f"which exceeds the target true peak of {self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak} dBTP. "
852                    "The loudnorm filter will likely use dynamic mode instead. "
853                    f"To avoid this, raise --true-peak (-tp) to at least {min_tp:.1f}, "
854                    f"or lower the target level (-t) to at most {max_target:.1f}."
855                )
856
857        # Adjust target level for batch mode to preserve relative loudness
858        if batch_reference is not None:
859            input_i = float(stats["input_i"])
860            # Formula: adjusted_target = target_level + (input_i - batch_reference)
861            # If track is quieter than average (input_i < batch_ref), offset is negative → quieter target
862            # If track is louder than average (input_i > batch_ref), offset is positive → louder target
863            adjusted_target = target_level + (input_i - batch_reference)
864            _logger.info(
865                f"Batch mode: Adjusting target from {target_level:.2f} to {adjusted_target:.2f} LUFS "
866                f"(input_i={input_i:.2f}, batch_ref={batch_reference:.2f}, offset={input_i - batch_reference:.2f})"
867            )
868            target_level = adjusted_target
869
870        opts = {
871            "i": target_level,
872            "lra": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.loudness_range_target,
873            "tp": self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.true_peak,
874            "offset": self._constrain(target_offset, -99, 99, name="target_offset"),
875            "measured_i": self._constrain(stats["input_i"], -99, 0, name="input_i"),
876            "measured_lra": self._constrain(
877                stats["input_lra"], 0, 99, name="input_lra"
878            ),
879            "measured_tp": self._constrain(stats["input_tp"], -99, 99, name="input_tp"),
880            "measured_thresh": self._constrain(
881                stats["input_thresh"], -99, 0, name="input_thresh"
882            ),
883            "linear": "false" if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dynamic else "true",
884            "print_format": "json",
885        }
886
887        if self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.dual_mono:
888            opts["dual_mono"] = "true"
889
890        self.verification_target_level = target_level
891        return "loudnorm=" + dict_to_filter_opts(opts)

Return second pass loudnorm filter options string for ffmpeg

Arguments:
  • batch_reference (float | None, optional): Reference loudness for batch mode. When provided, the target level is adjusted to preserve relative loudness. Defaults to None.
def get_second_pass_opts_peakrms(self, batch_reference: float | None = None) -> str: 
893    def get_second_pass_opts_peakrms(self, batch_reference: float | None = None) -> str:
894        """
895        Set the adjustment gain based on chosen option and mean/max volume,
896        return the matching ffmpeg volume filter.
897
898        Args:
899            batch_reference (float | None, optional): Reference loudness for batch mode.
900                When provided, the target level is adjusted to preserve relative loudness.
901                Defaults to None.
902
903        Returns:
904            str: ffmpeg volume filter string
905        """
906        if (
907            self.loudness_statistics["max"] is None
908            or self.loudness_statistics["mean"] is None
909        ):
910            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
911                "First pass not run, no mean/max volume to normalize to"
912            )
913
914        normalization_type = self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.normalization_type
915        target_level = self.media_file.ffmpeg_normalize.target_level
916
917        # Adjust target level for batch mode to preserve relative loudness
918        if batch_reference is not None:
919            if normalization_type == "peak":
920                measured_level = float(self.loudness_statistics["max"])
921            elif normalization_type == "rms":
922                measured_level = float(self.loudness_statistics["mean"])
923            else:
924                raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
925                    "Can only set adjustment for peak and RMS normalization"
926                )
927
928            # Formula: adjusted_target = target_level + (measured_level - batch_reference)
929            # If track is quieter than average (measured < batch_ref), offset is negative → quieter target
930            # If track is louder than average (measured > batch_ref), offset is positive → louder target
931            adjusted_target = target_level + (measured_level - batch_reference)
932            _logger.info(
933                f"Batch mode: Adjusting target from {target_level:.2f} to {adjusted_target:.2f} dB "
934                f"(measured={measured_level:.2f}, batch_ref={batch_reference:.2f}, offset={measured_level - batch_reference:.2f})"
935            )
936            target_level = adjusted_target
937
938        if normalization_type == "peak":
939            adjustment = 0 + target_level - self.loudness_statistics["max"]
940        elif normalization_type == "rms":
941            adjustment = target_level - self.loudness_statistics["mean"]
942        else:
943            raise FFmpegNormalizeError(
944                "Can only set adjustment for peak and RMS normalization"
945            )
946
947        _logger.info(
948            f"Adjusting stream {self.stream_id} by {adjustment} dB to reach {target_level}"
949        )
950
951        self.applied_gain = float(adjustment)
952
953        clip_amount = self.loudness_statistics["max"] + adjustment
954        if clip_amount > 0:
955            _logger.warning(
956                f"{self.media_file.input_file}: Adjusting will lead to clipping of {clip_amount} dB"
957            )
958
959        return f"volume={adjustment}dB"

Set the adjustment gain based on chosen option and mean/max volume, return the matching ffmpeg volume filter.

Arguments:
  • batch_reference (float | None, optional): Reference loudness for batch mode. When provided, the target level is adjusted to preserve relative loudness. Defaults to None.
Returns:

str: ffmpeg volume filter string

class MediaStream: 
102class MediaStream:
103    def __init__(
104        self,
105        ffmpeg_normalize: FFmpegNormalize,
106        media_file: MediaFile,
107        stream_type: Literal["audio", "video", "subtitle"],
108        stream_id: int,
109    ):
110        """
111        Create a MediaStream object.
112
113        Args:
114            ffmpeg_normalize (FFmpegNormalize): The FFmpegNormalize object.
115            media_file (MediaFile): The MediaFile object.
116            stream_type (Literal["audio", "video", "subtitle"]): The type of the stream.
117            stream_id (int): The stream ID.
118        """
119        self.ffmpeg_normalize = ffmpeg_normalize
120        self.media_file = media_file
121        self.stream_type = stream_type
